claims.title: Solute amount and water volume determine concentration during swelling
claims.statement: The change in concentration between two samples separates into a net amount change and dilution of the initial pool. Along a differentiable trajectory, the concentration slope depends on gross production minus gross loss and on the rate of volume change.
assumptions: Amount and water volume refer to the same compartment, and each volume is positive. The unit conversion between amount per volume and reported concentration is fixed.
For the rate identity, the amount and volume are differentiable at the observation time. The amount rate includes all routes of gain and loss for that pool.

To interpret the two gross rates separately requires another observation, such as a measured release or cohort tracer. Each comparison identifies which material and preparation the experiment followed.

numerical.result: On main 796f04fa the scheduled turnover operator refuses a changing volume at definition time. The native refusal control passed. A compiled replay of turnover with osmotic water awaits FR-65.

biology.observable: Amount and cell water in swelling preparations, and independently measured protein breakdown under lower osmolarity.
biology.unit: solute amount or released amino acid per g dry cells, water per g dry cells, or fractional change against each experiment’s baseline

evidence.citation: Meijer et al. (1993), Figs. 1–3 and Table 2
evidence.locator: Fig. 3E reports ATP amount. Fig. 3F calculates concentration from that amount and Fig. 1 cell water. Table 2 and Fig. 2B report valine production at 70 and 120 mM NaCl.
evidence.context: Isolated hepatocytes from fasted rats at 37 °C, with and without a physiological amino-acid mixture.
evidence.uncertainty: Cell water was measured at 45 min. The ATP difference is approximate. Table 2 reports mean ± SEM from 4 and 8 preparations at 70 and 120 mM NaCl.
evidence.assessment: Without added amino acids ATP amount rose slightly with swelling and calculated ATP concentration fell by up to about 10%. Both 90-minute valine means were 15.5 µmol/g dry cells. Adding amino acids inhibited proteolysis by about 40% versus 15% of the respective controls.

evidence.citation: Guizouarn et al. (2000), Fig. 1 and Table 1
evidence.locator: Table 1 gives the net changes from initial swelling to 60 min in the hypotonic bath. Fig. 1 gives the volume relative to the pre-shock value.
evidence.context: Rainbow-trout red cells transferred to 215 mOsm/kg with ouabain. Water and taurine were normalized to dry cell solids.
evidence.uncertainty: Means ± SEM from 21 experiments in the sodium bath and 3 in the potassium bath. No separate gross taurine production or loss was measured.
evidence.assessment: During recovery in the sodium bath, cells lost 42.97 ± 1.87 µmol taurine/g and 0.37 ± 0.02 g water/g. In the potassium bath they lost 37.30 ± 0.92 µmol taurine/g while gaining 0.06 ± 0.02 g water/g. This reuses the osmotic-water dataset.

evidence.locator: Fig. 1 and Methods, hypotonic perfusion at 185–275 mOsm/L against a 305 mOsm/L control.
evidence.context: Perfused livers from fed rats at 37 °C. The perfusate contained 0.1 mM unlabelled leucine. The authors followed leucine released from prelabelled liver proteins.
evidence.uncertainty: Water space and labelled leucine release were measured in separate liver series under matched protocols. Fig. 1 gives SEM with 3–15 experiments per point across conditions and includes some earlier same-group values.
evidence.assessment: Lowering perfusate osmolarity increased intracellular water and reduced labelled leucine release relative to baseline. The observable is protein breakdown in this preparation.

pairs.assumption: Hypo-osmotic swelling suppresses protein breakdown in rat liver preparations across amino-acid conditions.
pairs.independence: Separate research groups used perfused livers from fed animals and hepatocytes isolated from fasted animals. The measured products and amino-acid supply differed.
pairs.comparison: Labelled leucine release fell during hypotonic perfusion. In the isolated-cell no-added-amino-acid series, cumulative valine at 90 min was 15.5 ± 1.2 versus 15.5 ± 0.9 µmol/g dry cells (SEM). The physiological amino-acid mixture gave greater inhibition under hypotonic conditions.

replay.assessment: FR-65 remains open on main. These studies do not supply a common quantitative clearance rate across the two preparations.

pairs.assumption: Swelling changes the gross production and loss rates of the measured intracellular solute.
pairs.independence: Independent hepatocyte ATP and trout red-cell taurine experiments measured different solutes. The trout measurements also appear on the osmotic-water claim.
pairs.comparison: In hepatocytes calculated ATP concentration fell while ATP amount rose slightly. Trout cells lost taurine per g dry solids during volume recovery. Neither series separately measured production and loss of that solute.

replay.assessment: The proved identities relate concentration to the net amount and water volume. A joint compiled replay and independent gross-rate observations of the same solute remain open.

claims.title: An equilibrium channel blocker bounds flux sensitivity to voltage and concentration
claims.statement: The weighted fraction of unblocked channels lies between zero and one. Its absolute voltage derivative equals the native slope bound when the modes share a blocker side and charge sign. The product of this fraction and the free current obeys the native stage bound whenever the free current has the declared conductance bound. With the permeant ion’s reversal as reference, the inside and outside concentration bounds include how that ion changes both its free flux and the blocker fraction.
assumptions: Each mode has a positive dissociation constant at zero reference voltage. The blocker concentration is nonnegative. The finite mode weights are nonnegative and have positive total. Cells normalizes by the actual weight sum.

The voltage derivative holds concentration, temperature, availability and gate state fixed. The reference is membrane voltage or membrane voltage minus a fixed reversal potential. The native declaration assigns a single blocker side and charge sign to all modes.

Each concentration derivative fixes membrane voltage, blocker dose, gate state, temperature and the opposite endpoint. The permeant ion has nonzero signed valence, both endpoint concentrations are positive and the free flux has a nonnegative permeability scale.

A measured current ratio represents pore block only to the extent that changes in gating, driving force and the recording protocol are accounted for. Quantitative comparisons require a declared preparation, dose and voltage range.

numerical.result: The compiled CPU float64 clamp passed 6,543 in-range voltage checks across all 18 synthetic blocker cases on f8c6c326. The largest relative errors were 7.77 × 10⁻¹⁵ for the free fraction and 1.13 × 10⁻¹⁴ for the absolute blocker slope against the decimal reference. The largest full-current derivative was 0.989 of its bound or less. A four-mode automatic-differentiation control agreed to 1.90 × 10⁻¹³. All 15 native regression controls passed. On 796f04fa all 6,546 endpoint concentration bounds passed against the separately tagged reference. The smallest bound-to-derivative ratio was 0.9999999999999926 at 10⁻¹² relative tolerance. Both registered faults were detected, including a 192-fold shortfall after omission of the reversal term. A chloride control also passed at 37 voltages.

biology.observable: Change with voltage in the fraction of sodium current or permeability retained under external acidification. The nodal studies support the direction. The ventricular recordings cover a different voltage range. The exact derivative and transfer of mode parameters remain open.
biology.unit: relative sodium current or permeability at fixed voltage

evidence.locator: Fig. 4A and the summary, external pH 7 and 5.
evidence.context: Voltage-clamped frog nodes of Ranvier. The study estimated sodium permeability from peak current.
evidence.uncertainty: The two reductions are rounded examples. No pointwise uncertainty accompanies them in the summary. The +180 mV command is outside the native channel range.
evidence.assessment: Bath acidification reduced estimated permeability by about 60% at +20 mV and 20% at +180 mV. Block was relieved by stronger depolarization.

evidence.locator: Primary abstract, instantaneous nodal sodium-current measurements.
evidence.context: A separate group voltage-clamped nodal membranes at normal external pH and at pH 4.8–4.9. Instantaneous currents addressed open-channel block during acidification.
evidence.uncertainty: The abstract reports the direction. Pointwise responses, uncertainties and a common voltage interval were unavailable for this comparison.
evidence.assessment: Proton block decreased as membrane voltage became more positive. A shared numerical slope has yet to be tested.

evidence.locator: Fig. 3B and the single-channel amplitude analysis over −70 to −20 mV.
evidence.context: Native guinea-pig ventricular sodium channels, with extracellular pH 5.5 compared with 7.4. This assay measured unitary current amplitude.
evidence.uncertainty: This tissue, command interval and unitary-current readout differ from the nodal experiments. A zero slope cannot be inferred from an unresolved voltage effect.
evidence.assessment: Acid reduced unitary amplitude. The study found no significant voltage dependence of that reduction over its tested range, limiting extrapolation of the nodal result.

pairs.assumption: Depolarization relieves extracellular proton block of nodal sodium current.
pairs.independence: Woodhull’s original study motivated the model. The Mozhayeva group collected independent nodal recordings and used instantaneous currents to address gating. The comparison is the direction of voltage dependence.
pairs.comparison: Woodhull found about 40% versus 80% permeability retained at +20 versus +180 mV. The independent instantaneous-current study also found less block at more positive voltage. In ventricular myocytes, a separate unitary-current study resolved no slope over −70 to −20 mV.

replay.assessment: An extracellular positive blocker with positive electrical distance gives the observed direction at fixed dose. The synthetic engine comparison verifies the formula. A matched nodal current replay and common fitted slope remain open.

claims.title: A compartment wash accounts for each tracer label in the sample and the well
claims.statement: A well-mixed withdrawal of amount $r$ from a pool of amount $n$ collects $rs$ of a label with initial share $s$. The well keeps $(n-r)s$ and credits all the incoming unlabelled material to the base. For each label, the amount after the wash plus the collected amount equals its starting amount plus its refill.
assumptions: The finite set of declared labels includes the base. Starting shares are nonnegative and sum to one. The withdrawal is between zero and the starting amount, and the supply is nonnegative. Amounts use one common unit.

The event samples a well-mixed pool, with no preferential loss by label. An empty post-wash pool may retain bookkeeping shares that represent zero material. A complete exchange with positive refill puts every unit in the base.

For the dilution comparison the carrier concentration is the same before the wash and in its refill, which carries no tracer. Fixed volume makes the original-material concentration ratio equal to its fraction of the starting carrier. Reading fluorescence as this ratio also requires a linear optical response.

numerical.result: One compiled CPU float64 run on 3552e6cd applied twelve exchanges across four isolated wells. Each started with 1 fmol of tagged carrier. The largest absolute per-label balance residual was 4.44 × 10⁻¹⁶ fmol. The nine exchange controls and the compiled labelled/unlabelled twin regression also passed, including exact clearance of every non-base share on a whole wash with positive supply.

biology.observable: Normalized tracer signal in the retained liquid, paired with the amount of tracer in the withdrawal from the same exchange. The independent studies both measure dilution. A same-chamber assay of both inventories remains open.

evidence.locator: Fig. 2A shows the split, Fig. 4A the single-step concentrations, and supplement §S2 the adsorption check.
evidence.context: Aliquots of diverted stock and the diluted metered plug were assayed on the same chip using calibrated fluorescein fluorescence. The 5, 2 or 1 µL metered volumes were mixed downstream with 5, 8 or 9 µL of PBS.
evidence.uncertainty: Fig. 4A shows one SD with at least three replicates. The paper reports CV below 7%. Printed mean concentrations yield the ratios. The stored excess and downstream plug were sampled as aliquots, without total tracer recovery for the device.
evidence.assessment: The measured plug/stock ratios were 0.498, 0.193 and 0.093. The compiled equivalents were 0.500, 0.200 and 0.100. These are the same chip data already cited for the compartment-wash claim. Wall adsorption was measured.

evidence.locator: Fig. 3.6, printed p. 36. Markers run from zero to nine exchanges. At ten washes the figure has only a reference line.
evidence.context: A pipette replaced 20% of the solution in one PDMS chamber with pure water at each wash. Confocal imaging after equilibration measured fluorescein signal at one focal plane.
evidence.uncertainty: Graph readings are approximate to 0.01. Error bars denote SEM over three repeats, about 0.11 at wash one and 0.06 at wash five. The author discusses possible optical nonlinearity at late washes. No withdrawal assay was reported.
evidence.assessment: At washes one, five and nine the normalized signal was about 0.90, 0.21 and 0.05. Cells gave 0.800, 0.328 and 0.134. The late measured signal falls below the ideal concentration curve. The plotted reference matches 0.8ⁿ. Printed Eq. 3.7 would increase under the stated definition of the exchanged fraction.

pairs.assumption: Mixing retained fluorescein solution with tracer-free liquid lowers its normalized signal.
pairs.independence: KU Leuven measured split plugs. Durham independently imaged repeated exchanges in one chamber. The comparison is the direction of dilution.
pairs.comparison: Vloemans observed plug/stock ratios of 0.498, 0.193 and 0.093. Stubbington observed about 0.90 after one 20% wash and 0.05 after nine.

replay.assessment: The original-carrier concentration fell in all four compiled wells. Cells gave 0.500, 0.200 and 0.100 for the three plugs and 0.134 after nine chamber washes. The late chamber fluorescence lies below the prediction.

pairs.assumption: Tracer in the collected liquid and tracer left in the original chamber together account for the starting tracer after one well-mixed withdrawal and blank refill.
pairs.independence: These are the same two independent studies used for the dilution direction. Neither provides paired withdrawn and retained tracer amounts for one chamber exchange.
pairs.comparison: The chip assayed two concentrations after a split and downstream dilution. The chamber study followed the retained optical signal. Each lacks at least one measured inventory needed to close the experimental balance.

replay.assessment: The compiled run accounts for both inventories with a maximum discrepancy of 4.44 × 10⁻¹⁶ fmol. A quantitative comparison requires measured amounts and volumes on both sides of the same wash.

claims.title: Rounding and rejection of the initial charge balance
claims.statement: A balanced ionic inventory passes a closed charge tolerance T whenever T covers the accumulated rounding allowance E. A true charge error larger than T + E in magnitude is detected. At a midpoint in the 2²⁰-fmol range, rounding the fixed background alone can exceed the original 10⁻²⁰ C tolerance.
assumptions: The builder and reader use the same finite stored valence-weighted ion amounts and positive charge conversion in C/fmol. The builder forms the background by subtracting their rounded sum from the declared charge divided by the conversion.

Each arithmetic result satisfies its stated absolute error allowance. Four allowances are in fmol and the final two in coulombs. Half a local spacing bounds a nearest-grid result with either tie choice. The native replay checks each rounding premise against exact rational arithmetic for the sampled inputs.
A planted background change is its actual stored difference in fmol. The distinction between a genuine mismatch and rounding is guaranteed when their bounds are separated.

numerical.result: On 82c26ddd the native parser admitted all 15 balanced inputs and rejected both deliberately mischarged controls. The seven balanced refusals on cd3b7b09 and 8760d5b3 remain in the original record. Exact rational arithmetic verified all six local rounding allowances. Both signed midpoint controls had absolute residual 1.123237099 × 10⁻²⁰ C.

biology.observable: This arithmetic tolerance compares two calculations on the same declared inputs. An experimental test of the charge balance itself would need mobile and fixed charge, capacitance and potential from the same cell.

pairs.assumption: The sum of independently measured mobile and fixed charge in a native oocyte equals its capacitive charge.
pairs.independence: Guizouarn’s group assayed its own control oocytes. Costa’s group measured a separate set with ion-selective electrodes.
pairs.comparison: Guizouarn reported Na/K/Cl means of 30.0/115.2/21.2 mM, a pooled water estimate of about 500 nL per oocyte and a group voltage of −56.8 ± 1.5 mV. Costa estimated free-ion concentrations of 10.1/109.5/37.7 mM. Assay type and sampling differ. Evaluating charge closure requires total ion amounts, independently measured fixed charge, capacitance and voltage on the same cell. Neither series supplies that set.

replay.assessment: An independent fixed-charge amount, capacitance, total mobile charges and voltage from the same oocyte are missing. Numerical charge-closure controls cannot fill those measurements.

evidence.citation: Guizouarn et al. (2004), Table I, controls
evidence.locator: Experimental Procedures (ion and water measurements, electrophysiology) and Table I, noninjected controls.
evidence.context: Native Xenopus oocytes. Na and K measured by flame photometry, Cl by equilibrium tracer uptake, and membrane potential by electrodes.
evidence.uncertainty: Group means ± SE. The water estimate used pooled wet/dry weights and a trapped-water correction. Individual water uncertainty and overlap between the ion and voltage samples are unspecified.
evidence.assessment: The same group previously reported the −56.8 mV control (Table 1, 2001). These observations supply partial mobile-ion and voltage measurements. Treating a difference of their means as measured fixed charge would make the closure test circular.

evidence.locator: Summary, item 7, intracellular ion-selective microelectrode measurements.
evidence.context: Native Xenopus laevis oocytes, stages IV–V. Ion-selective electrodes estimated intracellular free ions on a concentration scale.
evidence.uncertainty: Separate sample counts per ion. The quoted equilibrium potentials for each species were calculated from concentrations. Those values cannot substitute for a measured membrane voltage in a charge balance.
evidence.assessment: The free-ion values give an independent scale for the three species. Converting activities to a total inventory additionally needs activity coefficients, binding and cell water. Fixed charge remains unmeasured.

claims.title: Integer units at membrane-patch division
claims.statement: At an accepted division, each occupied unit goes to exactly one daughter. The two counts recover the parent in every molecular state, the signed division entries balance, and the two daughters retain the parent's weighted subunit total.
assumptions: State counts are nonnegative integers in declaration order. The draw block covers all occupied units. The mapped daughters are distinct and empty before the parent retires. The first daughter receives units with a binary64 draw strictly below its patch-area share.
Each state's subunit weight is fixed. The expected sister-count differences additionally assume intact units with independent draws and one common first-daughter probability within each division.

numerical.result: On FR-43 development engine 9663f28f, the compiled division matched independently reconstructed counts and signed entries for four parent sites at all six saved times. The weighted daughter pairs were (4, 3), (6, 0), (3, 1) and (0, 0). Volume share, a tie sent to the first daughter and reversed state order gave 3, 1 and 2 incorrect first-daughter entries respectively, while each alternative still conserved total counts. The lead’s registered equal-share run at 52935908 gave 4,058 first-daughter assignments in 8,192 trials and passed its frequency check. [Cells decision D319](https://github.com/Eidosoma/Cells/blob/ac8d915ccefebd31d6357c5ddc0ff4dfc2b39f31/docs/DECISIONS.md#L10061)

biology.observable: Intact units counted in the parent and both daughters at cleavage, with the membrane-patch area inherited by each daughter measured in the same division.
biology.finding: One fission-yeast division preserves the visible focus count. The four-focus cohort split more evenly on average than the independent-allocation expectation for any common daughter probability. These cytoplasmic measurements leave membrane-area-dependent segregation open.

evidence.locator: Upper-left dividing cell, movie labels 120 and 130 min.
evidence.context: Hsp104-GFP marks visible cytoplasmic protein aggregates in fission yeast. The parent's one visible focus gives the predicted sum of daughter counts.
evaluation: Visible count before and in both daughters after the same division
evidence.uncertainty: One image pair. Subthreshold foci and individual protein copy numbers are unresolved.
evidence.assessment: The larger daughter inherited one visible focus and the smaller daughter inherited zero. This observation supports count conservation in that division.

evidence.locator: Green experimental series, groups with two and four visible foci at division.
evidence.context: The observable is the mean absolute difference between the sisters' focus counts. For four intact units with independent allocation, 1.5 is the smallest expected difference over all common daughter probabilities. For two units the minimum is 1.
evaluation: Four foci at division, 32 divisions, reported below
evidence.uncertainty: Mean differences and SEMs are approximate readings from the plot. The SEM is about 0.18 visible foci in each group. Membrane area fractions paired with these counts were unavailable.
evidence.assessment: Two foci gave about 0.97 against the equal-share expectation of 1. Four gave about 1.0 against the minimum expectation of 1.5. Aggregate fusion and spatial confinement limit transfer of this comparison to membrane units.

claims.title: Two processes spending and replenishing one finite pool
claims.statement: The change in a shared stock equals the sum of the two writers’ signed bookings over any interval, including a tail after restart. An independently measured reserve with known stoichiometry can distinguish their contributions. A common standard potential assigns a single standard-energy change to the stock.
assumptions: Each writer books exactly its own signed amount change. Both use the same amount units, preserve the cumulative counters at restart and account for every source or sink in this interval. The reserve used to infer one writer’s contribution has no other active route.

For the two rate probes, the numerator is nonzero at held amounts and controls and volume is positive. The stale-volume energy identity applies to positive amounts in an ideal mixture and compares the same change in amount at two volumes.

numerical.result: On the FR-43 part 2B development revision 211a9c17, the fixed-volume network added 0.004997501 fmol and the gene unit spent a net 0.000664664 fmol. The 5 s disk restart reproduced all 78 state fields. Shifting 1% of a writer’s booking to its partner preserved the total and failed the independent reserve check. In a swelling cell both rate probes agreed at 2 and 3 s within 2.54 × 10⁻⁶ relative error. Supplying the initial volume to one writer at a time identified that writer in each control. These checks cover the saved-state rates and accounts. On main b06158e8 and cd3b7b09, all four replays gave byte-identical results, including the 78-field restart and both stale-volume controls. The registered part 2 coupled-trajectory comparisons also passed (D324, D328).

biology.observable: A finite nucleotide pool, its upstream reserve and its consumption product measured together. For a changing-volume amount balance, each concentration also needs a matched volume.
biology.finding: Under a common-volume assumption, the five archived metabolite means allow a check of net UTP supply and spending. Measurement independence, uncertainty of the full residual and gross reaction rates remain open. In a separate rat hepatocyte study, swelling slightly increased ATP amount while the concentration calculated from measured cell-water volume fell. This directly illustrates the importance of the volume denominator. [Meijer et al., Figures 1 and 3E–F](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1432-1033.1993.tb18053.x)

evidence.locator: Figure 8 validation batch, 40_TO7h mean and SD tables. The archived samples span 0 to 24 h.
evidence.context: The reconstruction assumes a common volume and that all uridine remains in the five measured pools. It uses upstream depletion, product accumulation and the initial UTP, with no fitted rates. The Figure 8 code reads processed means. The public files do not document the conversion from chromatographic peaks to those means. [Figure 8 data reader](https://github.com/klamt-lab/MoRSel_UDP-GalNAc_Paper/blob/3a6ae20eb9c33bf667f4af9c1942cc4f4fce2963/process_optimization/visualize_selected_predictions.py#L19-L123)
evaluation: All nine UTP means from 0.5 to 24 h, with the 7 h measurement reported below
evidence.uncertainty: Reported UTP SD at 7 h is 0.350096 mM. The three archived replicate pairs contain baseline uridine and 7 h product. The other contributors to the residual have marginal SDs, leaving the uncertainty of the full balance unresolved. [Paired measurements](https://github.com/klamt-lab/MoRSel_UDP-GalNAc_Paper/blob/3a6ae20eb9c33bf667f4af9c1942cc4f4fce2963/process_optimization/exp_val_data/UDP-GalNAc40_TO7h_biol_repl_data.txt)
evidence.assessment: At 7 h the upstream pools supplied a net 38.101943 mM and product accumulation spent 37.279854 mM. Predicted minus observed UTP ranged from −0.284381 to +0.276418 mM across the nine samples. At 24 h the reconstruction gave 0.697341 mM against 0.525149 mM observed with a UTP SD of 0.021942 mM. This SD covers only the measured UTP channel.

claims.title: Rosenbrock reaction steps preserve closed material inventories
claims.statement: A weighted sum of species amounts that balances each reaction is preserved by every exact Rosenbrock stage solve, by the accepted endpoint and throughout the Rodas4 dense polynomial used to locate crossings.
assumptions: The field is differentiable near the starting state. The inventory is linear and each stoichiometric change balances it at every stage. The fixed Jacobian is the derivative of that field, the scalar shift is nonzero and the stage equations are solved exactly.
The inventory covers a closed reaction interval. Reservoir transfers, boundary events and changes of representation require their own bookkeeping.

numerical.result: In a closed A + B ⇌ C run, A+C and B+C started at 11,000 and 3,000 molecule units. The first accepted endpoint matched the first saved row bit for bit. All six stages and five dense samples preserved both totals within float64 rounding. Across 64 accepted steps the four saved observations had a maximum relative drift of 9.10 × 10⁻¹⁶ against the native 10⁻¹² tolerance. The unweighted molecule count changed by 653.29.

pairs.assumption: G6P and F6P alone form a closed measured inventory throughout these enzyme assays.
pairs.independence: Kahana’s group assayed a partially purified preparation. Eicher’s group measured a separate cell extract capable of additional reactions.
pairs.comparison: The purified assay recovered 2.505 of the initial 2.500 mM at 30 min. Eicher’s dataset 2 lost 22.29% of the measured sum, while dataset 3 gained 1.04%. Recovery error and unmeasured species prevent treating the extract as a matched closed pool. These data cannot establish a failure of the integration invariant.

replay.assessment: Cells preserves the sum for a closed pair. Closure of the experimental extract and recovery of all relevant material have not been established.

biology.observable: Total soluble glucose-6-phosphate and fructose-6-phosphate during their reversible interconversion.
biology.finding: A partially purified enzyme preparation recovered approximately the starting total. One cell-extract time course lost 22.29% of the measured pair. Recovery uncertainty and the disposition of material outside the pair are unresolved.

evidence.citation: Kahana et al. (1960), Table II, experiment B
evidence.locator: Table II, experiment B, 0, 15 and 30 minutes. Figure 3 describes the assay conditions.
evidence.context: Partially purified rabbit-muscle PGI at 30 °C and pH 8.0. Cells starts at the positive 15-minute pair and advances 900 s. Its conserved total is independent of the kinetic parameters.
evidence.uncertainty: The concentrations share a sequential absorbance assay. The paper reports rounded concentrations without a replicate uncertainty for their sum.
evidence.assessment: The measured totals were 2.500, 2.500 and 2.505 mM. The final value exceeds the closed-pair prediction by 0.005 mM (0.2%).

evidence.citation: Eicher et al. (2012), Fig. 5 and PGI worksheet
evidence.locator: Unsmoothed PGI worksheet, F4:H4 to F33:H33 and K4:M4 to K29:M29.
evidence.context: The same two E. coli K-12 extract courses at 25 °C and pH 7.2 also supply the reaction-direction comparison. Here the observable is the sum of both sugars.
evidence.uncertainty: The workbook gives no pointwise uncertainty or covariance. Neither course measures material outside the soluble pair.
evidence.assessment: Dataset 2 fell from 6.8872 to 5.3523 mM (−22.29%). Dataset 3 rose from 9.5845 to 9.6838 mM (+1.04%). Conservation of the two measured sugars in the extract is unresolved.

claims.title: A size-triggered division preserves each membrane species across both daughter records
claims.statement: Ranking the occupied membrane places gives a daughter of size k and a sibling of size N − k. When 0 < k < N, each daughter starts below the parent’s threshold. Their per-species counts sum to the parent’s.
assumptions: One membrane molecule occupies each ranked place. A join reaches the trigger at N, the partition selects the first k places, and the sibling receives the complement.

k is the integer obtained by flooring the engine’s binary64 product of the configured fraction and N. The proof takes the realized rank, including a stable ordering of tied uniforms, and the proper integer quota as inputs.
The first daughter continues and the second goes to the discard sink. The claim covers the membrane species array. Held pools have their own accounting.

numerical.result: All 30 divisions in 300 exact events matched the independent trace and rank reconstruction. At threshold 15, the two daughters kept 6 and 9 membrane molecules. All three species, every continued-daughter row and 89 discard transfers matched. Two tied-rank controls selected the expected species at the boundary.

biology.observable: Parent and paired daughter membrane counts by species at an independently observed growth threshold.
biology.unit: dimensionless diameter ratio for the geometric comparison

evidence.locator: Figure 3a and its accompanying text, 152 pairs. Figure 4a from the same paper supplies the separate lumen-dye comparison under vesicle shear fission.
evidence.context: Mechanically divided liposomes at a microfluidic Y-junction. Each pair contributes the smaller daughter diameter divided by the larger.
evidence.uncertainty: The paper reports 0.03 as the standard deviation of the diameter ratio across pairs.
evidence.assessment: The diameters describe approximate geometric symmetry. The size-triggered operator specifies molecule counts. The experiment leaves the growth threshold and membrane inventory of each daughter unmeasured.

claims.title: RNA detachment books its free-energy drop once
claims.statement: Each physical release fate books nonnegative heat throughout the active domain. An inactive fate books zero even while its amount changes through degradation. With concurrent synthesis, release and degradation, the sum of the three heats cancels the total free-energy change.
assumptions: At fixed temperature and volume, fate and held RNA share a standard energy per molecule at 1 M. Both endpoints of an active fate are positive and at or below the domain limit.

The finite-step chemical potential is the divided difference of the row’s ideal free energy. At equal amounts it is the derivative. Each nonnegative detachment uses its physical fate’s potential. The durable fraction may be anywhere in [0,1].
The same signed extents change the hold, the receiving and degraded rows and the corresponding heat classes. The fixed-temperature balance here has no external work.

numerical.result: The maximum isolated heat discrepancy was 4.36 × 10⁻²² pJ over 18 compiled rows. Under synthesis and degradation the largest full balance error across 60 half-steps was 3.83 × 10⁻¹⁹ pJ. Forty inactive fate half-steps had ongoing loss and exactly zero release heat. Equal release and loss in a separate component move booked positive heat at unchanged amount.

biology.observable: An independently constrained chemical-potential drop per detached RNA in a defined physical fate at measured activities and temperature. The available RNA release curves measure timing and amounts.

claims.title: Zero outer current preserves combined matrix and intermembrane-space charge
claims.statement: At fixed compartment water volumes the change in total matrix and intermembrane-space row charge equals the signed charge admitted through the outer membrane. A conducting passive face has a unique zero-current voltage. The initial inventory needs an intermembrane-space charge as well as a matrix charge.
assumptions: Sum all species with their physical valences, including charge redistributed by internal redox and binding. There is no hidden counter-ion, external current source or outer-membrane capacitive charge.
The seven inner-cycle columns conserve charge across both sides. Additional internal reactions must also conserve charge.

The passive single-face uniqueness result uses positive total charged conductance. Zero outer voltage at the anchor and start is the G5 initialization rule. Later voltages follow the current constraint.

numerical.result: In two compiled seven-cycle worlds with a potassium-only outer face, combined charge changed by at most 1.27 × 10⁻¹⁸ fmol of charge equivalents. Initial IMS-minus-bath voltage was 0 mV at matched K and −85.61293 mV at a 140:5 gradient. The original outer face admitted K and AMP individually and refused five other declared rows. The forms-aware law now has a [separate transport comparison](forms-face-carriage.md). The full MT-1b anchor/start comparison remains open.

biology.observable: Intermembrane-space and bath voltage in the isolated mitochondrial preparation at the declared anchor and start, together with valence-weighted inventories.
biology.unit: mV from IMS to external reference and fmol of charge equivalents

evidence.locator: Figure 1E, equation 1 and accompanying Results.
evidence.context: In intact cells from a human cell line, compartment-targeted measurements gave mean bulk IMS pH 7.96 and mean cytosolic pH 7.41. The authors inferred +33 ± 11 mV, positive on the IMS side.
evidence.uncertainty: The pH observations have reported SDs of 0.08 (IMS) and 0.17 (cytosol). Converting the gradient to voltage assumes proton equilibrium.
evidence.assessment: The cellular gradient makes the compartment definition consequential. It leaves the voltage of isolated mitochondria in their declared bath and the initial combined charge unmeasured.

claims.title: Deterministic reactions stall at equilibrium and dissipate free energy
claims.statement: An enabled reaction with positive forward factor has forward flux exactly when its reservoir-adjusted free-energy change is negative, reverse flux when positive, and zero flux at equilibrium. The instantaneous dissipation is nonnegative for every reaction and for any finite sum.
assumptions: The driving force is the stoichiometric change in chemical potential minus reservoir work, in units of k_BT. The enabled forward factor is finite and nonnegative. An inactive reaction or zero forward factor has zero flux for every finite force.

The theorem concerns the instantaneous constitutive equation over the reals. Accuracy of the time integrator, floating-point evaluation and agreement with a particular assay each require separate evidence.

numerical.result: The two compiled reaction fluxes matched independent linear rates within 1.10 × 10⁻¹¹ events/s across five states, including relative changes of 10⁻⁹ on each side of exact stall. Both padded slots returned zero. At 4 mM product with a 2 mM reservoir, omitting the reservoir work reversed the predicted direction.

pairs.assumption: Phosphoglucose isomerase can convert G6P to F6P or F6P to G6P, depending on the starting mixture.
pairs.independence: Eicher’s group measured cell-extract time courses by NMR. Dyson and Noltmann independently assayed purified rabbit-muscle enzyme.
pairs.comparison: F6P fell by 3.787 mM in the F6P-start extract series and rose by 1.172 mM in the G6P-start series. The purified enzyme approached F6P/G6P ≈ 0.30 from both sides. Both assays support the direction of conversion. Instantaneous dissipation remains unmeasured.

replay.assessment: The extract’s starting compositions give opposite native flux signs. At the purified enzyme’s temperature and kinetic equilibrium estimate, the native zero is near the endpoint reached from either side. Absolute heat was unmeasured.

biology.observable: Direction of glucose-6-phosphate (G6P) and fructose-6-phosphate (F6P) conversion from opposite starting conditions, the equilibrium ratio, and dissipated heat per unit time.
biology.finding: Two extract time courses changed in the directions given by their fitted equilibrium. A separate rabbit-muscle equilibrium assay lets us compare a zero-flux ratio inferred from kinetics with a measured endpoint.

evidence.locator: PGI worksheet, F4:H4 and F33:H33 in dataset 2, K4:M4 and K29:M29 in dataset 3.
evidence.context: E. coli K-12 extract in 100 mM PIPES at pH 7.2 and 25 °C. The model uses the authors’ fitted ratio of 0.286 for these same courses.
evidence.uncertainty: The stored unsmoothed concentrations have no per-point error estimates. The two tubes share a date and nominal protocol. A common extract batch is unverified.
evidence.assessment: F6P fell by 3.787 mM in the F6P-start tube and rose by 1.172 mM in the G6P-start tube. Cells matched both net directions. The time courses leave instantaneous heat unmeasured.

evidence.citation: Dyson and Noltmann (1968), Table I and Fig. 13
evidence.locator: Table I reports kinetic and equilibrium determinations. Figure 13 describes the approaches from both sugars.
evidence.context: Purified rabbit-muscle enzyme at 30 °C, pH 8.5 and ionic strength 0.12. The model sets the standard-potential difference from the authors’ kinetic estimate.
fit: Equilibrium ratio inferred from the forward and reverse kinetic parameters
evaluation: Equilibrium composition measured in the same preparation starting from either sugar
evidence.uncertainty: Table I supplies no uncertainty for the measured equilibrium ratio.
evidence.assessment: The compiled stall ratio exceeds the measured endpoint by 0.020. Statistical agreement remains unassessed.

claims.title: Vesicle area variation bounds survival during a tension hold
claims.statement: Under a common hazard per unit area, survival evaluated at the initial mean area bounds the cohort’s survival from below. The linear interpolation of the two endpoint survivals at that mean bounds it from above. An endpoint mixture attains the upper bound.
assumptions: Every vesicle has fixed area during observation, the same integrated hazard per unit area and single-vesicle survival exp(−qA). The initial finite cohort weights are nonnegative and sum to one.

For the upper bound, L and U are actual limits on the same initial cohort’s areas and L < U. If L = U the common single-area result is exact. Positive exposure and unequal areas with positive weights give a strict lower bound.

For spherical vesicles the required mean area is 4π times the mean of squared radii. Inferring area from a mean radius alone requires further information. D293’s set-2 allowance addresses area differences across preparations. The bound here concerns the survival curve within one cohort.

numerical.result: Four synthetic checks cover distinct and identical areas and zero exposure. At one second, two equally weighted founders in the compiled shared-pool runner give 0.3577327717421851 from their recorded hazards. The mean-area lower bound is 0.3561630590540235 and the upper chord is 0.3577327717421859. The calculation uses rate-implied probabilities.

biology.observable: Initial vesicle areas from the same at-risk population, held tension, and time to first rupture or censoring per vesicle. Linked observations would quantify the mean-area approximation.
biology.unit: Surviving fraction at a stated exposure

evidence.locator: Figure 4A, with Figure 4B as the pre-equilibrium comparison
evidence.context: Neutral DOPC vesicles at 25 ± 1 °C, held at 4 mN/m aspiration after a 3 mM osmotic difference.
evidence.uncertainty: The paper gives 0.0086 ± 0.0002 for fractional plateau radius change (17 vesicles), without identifying the statistic here. The mean area modulus is 218 ± 26 mN/m (SD).
evidence.assessment: Relative radius and rupture are paired on displayed traces. Individual absolute areas and complete event or censor times are still missing.

evidence.citation: Saha, Shibly and Yamazaki (2020), Journal of Physical Chemistry B
evidence.locator: Figure 1B and Table 1 for rupture, Figure 2 and Table 3 for swelling
evidence.context: DOPG/DOPC 40:60 vesicles in 150 mM NaCl at 25 ± 1 °C. The rupture group used 12 mOsm/L and the closest swelling group used 13 ± 5 mOsm/L.
evidence.uncertainty: Rates are means and SDs of 4–5 repeats, each with 20–25 vesicles. Geometry-based osmotic tension at 13 mOsm/L was 3.0 ± 0.1 mN/m. The ±5 mOsm/L is estimated osmolarity error.
evidence.assessment: Rupture rate rose 6.52-fold over the applied 3.5–4.5 mN/m range. The independent swelling estimate comes from a different cohort. Rate-matched tension uses the rupture data themselves.

biology.finding: Shibly et al. link relative swelling and rupture in selected neutral-DOPC traces. Saha et al. compare charged-vesicle rupture and swelling in separate cohorts. Neither supplies absolute starting areas with outcomes across the full at-risk cohort.

claims.title: A finite error bound for survival after an RNA release window
claims.statement: For a positive measured count at window close, a proposed survival fraction can be checked against the two counts. The change in the later count contributes its absolute error and the uncertainty in the close count contributes that error times the proposed fraction.
assumptions: The same cohort is followed through the chase, with common nonnegative survival factors and no new members. Their product is the expected ratio.

Both count uncertainties bound absolute errors in the same amount unit. The engine estimates these from a coarser grid. A missing estimate leaves the numerical comparison unresolved, and an empty cohort has no survival ratio.

numerical.result: All six controls met their expected verdicts and the independent reader reproduced all eight saved development readouts on Cells 4944314d. At zero count-grid error the valid 0.25000000000000006 turnover ratio passes with a ratio-rounding allowance of 7.105427357601002 × 10⁻¹⁵. The changed-rate control at 0.5 still fails. The earlier false refusal and its record remain linked. The registered FR-38 outcome remains R1 failed and R2 inconclusive.

biology.observable: The same release-marked molecules counted at the end of the window and again after the chase, with uncertainties on both counts.

claims.title: Marked RNA is accounted for in both release fates, including after label reuse
claims.statement: A detachment event marked in a half-open window belongs to exactly one of the two fates. In the continuous-amount model their gross amounts sum to the marked release even when the split changes. Each fate can have its own survival fraction. Reusing a label adds the survivors of both windows, and the chase fraction uses the original cohort alive at window close.
assumptions: Time is indexed by step boundaries. In the exact event example a molecule is marked on detachment and experiences the following interval’s survival factor. Sampling is before any new releases at that sample boundary.

Every member of the same physical pool experiences the same survival factor in each interval. For a physical chase each factor is in [0,1]. A reused label receives new material from nonoverlapping windows.

A zero denominator gives an undefined chase fraction. A host readout with only interval totals assumes a within-interval arrival profile. The synthetic counter comparison uses uniform arrivals and constant per-molecule loss.
Gross release is nonnegative. The durable fraction p lies in [0,1] and can vary by step. The short-lived fraction is 1 − p. Each fate has a survival fraction in [0,1].

numerical.result: Across three compiled RNA runs all 39 physical readouts matched bit for bit. The two marked intervals released 1.02212491320 × 10⁻¹⁰ fmol into the two fates. Reusing a label reproduced the sum of the two separately marked cohorts to within 1.30 × 10⁻²⁶ fmol. The counter reconstruction’s maximum relative error for the short-lived fate was 4.80 × 10⁻⁸ on a two-second output grid and 2.93 × 10⁻⁹ on a half-second grid. The independent point-release example retained 6 of 8 at chase. The separate FR-42 tissue comparison checked the same window semantics with production and clearance. This window comparison followed the same producer throughout. A separate [producer replacement and restart comparison](producer-replacement-rna.md) follows both generations on the development engine.

biology.observable: Cohort membership requires the time of release from the template and survival of the same molecules to a later sample.
biology.finding: Bellecourt et al. measured detachment among terminator-length RNAs. Ntini et al. measured chromatin association after a synthesis pulse, and Tutucci et al. counted yeast RNA during mitosis. A direct survival comparison still requires marking RNA at detachment and measuring the same cohort at window close and during chase.

evidence.citation: Bellecourt et al. (2019), Journal of Molecular Biology 431, 696–713
evidence.locator: Figure 5A and accompanying Results, with the time course in Figure S5
evidence.context: In vitro bacterial transcription. The assay distinguished released terminator-length RNA and template-associated terminator-length RNA. The chase followed labelling of nascent RNA.
evidence.uncertainty: The study reports ±0.02 for the wild-type release fraction under reducing conditions. Figure 5A pools the 120, 240 and 480 s samples.
evidence.assessment: This measures population detachment. Individual completion-to-release delays and later survival of the same released cohort remain unmeasured.

evidence.locator: Figure 1, GEO GSE218726 and the authors’ transcript table, ACTB row ENSG00000075624.14.
evidence.context: After an eight-minute synthesis pulse in MCF-7 cells, RNA was measured in chromatin and nucleoplasmic fractions at 0, 5, 10, 15 and 20 minutes.
evidence.uncertainty: The transcript table gives a point estimate for this row.
evidence.assessment: ACTB’s fitted chromatin-association half-time was 3.35 min. Each denominator pools the two recovered nuclear fractions. Relating these fractions to survival after detachment would require the size and subsequent fate of a cohort marked at release.

evidence.locator: Figure 6b–c. The group estimate comes from panel c.
evidence.context: Endogenously tagged ASH1 RNA spots were counted per cell in 21 yeast cells every two minutes, with times aligned to anaphase onset.
evidence.uncertainty: The authors report ±2.8 min with the 6.1 min value. The type of uncertainty is unspecified.
evidence.assessment: The mitotic decline in detected ASH1 spots had a reported half-life of 6.1 min. A per-cell count gives a population decay timescale. The release time and subsequent survival of a detachment-marked cohort remain unmeasured.

evidence.locator: Fig. 2A and Supplementary Fig. S2.
evidence.context: New reporter RNA was assayed after removal of extracellular 4-thiouridine.
evidence.uncertainty: Timing is specific to this preparation. Intracellular nucleotide-triphosphate concentration was not measured.
evidence.assessment: Incorporation continued after medium exchange and became negligible after about one hour.

evidence.locator: Fig. 5A–B, incorporation following the label switch.
evidence.context: Sequencing distinguished old-label-only and double-labelled transcripts during a metabolic-label switch.
evidence.uncertainty: The increased cumulative signal over that interval does not give the instantaneous incorporation rate at its endpoint.
evidence.assessment: Old-label-only transcript signal increased during the first two hours after the switch. The result supports continued incorporation during this window.

pairs.assumption: Removing the extracellular labelled nucleotide precursor immediately ends incorporation of the old label into newly made RNA.
pairs.independence: The two groups independently measured newly labelled RNA with different nucleotide analogues and readouts.
pairs.comparison: Residual incorporation of the labelled precursor became negligible after about an hour in the reporter assay. Old-label-only signal accumulated during the first two hours of the metabolic-label switch in the second assay.

replay.assessment: Cells starts its cohort clock at the recorded event. Mapping a medium switch to that clock requires the precursor incorporation history. Neither experiment measured an intracellular triphosphate decay constant or a universal clearance time.

claims.title: Neutral arrival-time cohorts share one physical loss rate
claims.statement: Allocating one well-mixed population’s loss among cohorts in proportion to their amounts preserves the total loss, the total after one step, and readouts evaluated on those pooled totals. For quadratic loss, a tracked cohort and the difference from an independently evolved blank can give different answers.
assumptions: The finite inventory includes the unlabelled remainder. The physical rate J(N) is computed once on the total N, with J(0) = 0. A cohort of size n receives J(N)·n/N for an occupied pool and zero for an empty pool.
The step identity uses a common step size. Applying the readout identity to energy or heat requires the engine to evaluate these quantities from the physical pool.
The exact example starts with two old units and one new unit, with no further arrivals, and uses N′ = −N². The comparison blank begins with only the two old units.

numerical.result: Five quadratic-loss pools kept their shares bit for bit. At one second, the three-unit pool held 0.7499996135 fmol including 0.2499998712 fmol from the new cohort, within 10⁻⁶ fmol of 3/4 and 1/4. The analytical two-unit blank gives a difference of 1/12 fmol. All 42 shared history fields and 76 shared observations, including energy records, matched bit for bit when labels were enabled. Diagnostics agreed. In FR-49 World L the labelled and unlabelled twins also matched on shared physics beside a compartment. The development replay on cd3b7b09 adds label arrival, local expression exclusions and a 900 s restart through 1,260 s. A paired owner–compartment transfer proof remains open.

biology.observable: The surviving fraction of an identified arrival cohort within the same physical pool, paired with that pool’s total at the observation time.
biology.finding: In mock-treated mouse dendritic cells the 5 h Actn1 heavy fractions were 17.19% and 10.11%. The paired channel sum supplies the denominator. Recycling limits how precisely the heavy fraction measures newly made protein. For RNA pulse–chase assays, old nucleotide can still enter new RNA after a medium switch. Mapping that switch to a defined arrival cohort requires the incorporation history. [Pendleton, Fig. 2](https://rnajournal.cshlp.org/content/24/6/778.full) · [Gasser, Fig. 5](https://doi.org/10.1002/anie.201916272)

evidence.locator: Figure 1B, Figure 3F and GEO GSE59792, Actn1, paired 5 h MOCK medium and heavy samples.
evidence.context: Pulse SILAC after an isotope switch in mouse dendritic cells. The four samples have proteome-normalized iBAQ signals.
evidence.uncertainty: Sample SD 0.050071 across the two paired fractions. Both isotope channels were present in both replicates.
evidence.assessment: Within-replicate normalization cancels in H/(H+M). Its denominator is computed from the same two measurements. Recycled precursor can enter newly made protein. A common loss rate and the quadratic-loss example remain untested by this measurement.

claims.title: A positive endpoint determines one neutral-label survival exponent
claims.statement: With nonnegative old stock and gross arrivals, every positive endpoint up to their sum has exactly one nonnegative loss exponent. At that exponent the label amounts are nonnegative, sum to the endpoint and give shares that sum to one. An occupied pool receiving no arrivals keeps its shares.
assumptions: One well-mixed physical pool has a common constant per-molecule loss rate and constant arrival rates per label during the step. The dimensionless exponent is the loss rate times the step duration.
Initial shares are nonnegative, include all material, and sum to one. Gross arrivals into each label are nonnegative. At zero loss all old material and all arrivals survive.
The inferred exponent describes one step in exact arithmetic. A completely empty pool cannot identify a rate. Inferring a rate over multiple steps with varying loss or arrivals is a separate problem.

numerical.result: NumPy and CPU JAX recovered eight constructed exponents from 0 to 1,000 within 2 × 10⁻¹⁴ absolute plus 2 × 10⁻¹³ relative tolerance. The largest absolute share error was 1.11 × 10⁻¹⁶. An empty-row control kept its stored shares. Seven cell-cohort observations in the compiled world agreed with the constant-rate integral within 2.78 × 10⁻¹⁷ fmol.

biology.observable: Independent gross arrivals, physical pool amounts at the two step endpoints, and survivor amounts for each labelled cohort under a common constant loss rate.
biology.unit: Amount per cohort and physical pool in a shared unit

claims.title: Daughter rupture at birth can be reconstructed from the shear records
claims.statement: Each retained daughter that ruptures returns its contents once. A single-lineage shear records the pool before the followed daughter releases. A population shear records the pool after all releases at that stop. Subtracting the finite receipts and adding back the signed reservoir debits recovers the starting balances.
assumptions: Each daughter and each of its source places appears once with a nonnegative count. Its key identifies it across the stop, including when siblings from different parents occupy the same slot in succession. The recorded rupture and continuation flags determine which daughters release.

Every source place has one pool destination for its species. Its finite or held status stays fixed. Division itself leaves the pool unchanged, and the earlier and later records bound the same shear event.
Only retained daughters that rupture credit the modeled pool. An unfollowed daughter leaves the single-lineage system through its sink.

numerical.result: Six compiled runs checked finite and held returns, an unfollowed rupture, consecutive daughters in a reused slot and two releases from one three-way split. An archived OL5 population shear independently supplied seven release rows. The finite lipid pool rose from 270 to 2,359, the solute pool from 0 to 55,631, and signed held lipid supply fell by 356.

biology.observable: Tracer in the parent, each daughter and the surrounding liquid at an identified division with one ruptured daughter.
biology.finding: Deshpande et al. observed one daughter surviving as its sibling ruptured at a microfluidic Y-junction. The paper also reports paired sibling signals in successful divisions and external dye spreading averaged across events. The amount released to the bath by the identified daughter remains unmeasured in this comparison. [Sibling fates, Fig. 1d](https://ceesdekkerlab.nl/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Mechanical-division-of-cell-sized-liposomes.pdf#page=2) · [Sibling signals, Fig. 3b](https://ceesdekkerlab.nl/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Mechanical-division-of-cell-sized-liposomes.pdf#page=5) · [External dye, Fig. 4](https://ceesdekkerlab.nl/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Mechanical-division-of-cell-sized-liposomes.pdf#page=6)

claims.title: Terminal rupture accounts once for every molecule returned to its destination
claims.statement: Starting at the triggering step’s own pool, each finite pool gains the molecules returned to it. Each held pool keeps its count and its signed reservoir supply decreases by the receipt. Summing the receipts over destinations accounts for the entire contents of the ruptured vesicle.
assumptions: The source list is the membrane and lumen places of the ruptured vesicle. Each appears once with its nonnegative count after the triggering step. Each has exactly one destination pool for its species.
The pool state used as the starting point already includes the triggering step. A destination has a fixed finite or held status during release. Counts lie in the engine’s admitted integer domain.
The four comparisons use step-triggered lysis. A population lysis row belongs to the affected slot at that event. The held tracer in these fixtures has no other route for exchange.

numerical.result: Four saved CPU runs reconciled by destination in single-lineage and population modes. Four membrane lipids and two lumen lipids returned to a pool holding one lipid, giving seven. Two impermeant tracers returned to a finite pool or reduced held supply by two with 9.210340371976182 kT of return work.

biology.observable: Paired counts in a vesicle and each recipient immediately across complete rupture, including the material recovered outside.

claims.title: The osmotic energy of a vesicle event is independent of its path
claims.statement: The incremental change equals the difference between the final and initial equilibrium energies for both membrane regimes and both crossing directions. A forward event followed by its exact reverse has zero net osmotic energy.
assumptions: The lumen count, membrane footprint, bath density, molecular standard and footprint-to-volume coefficient are positive. Bath and standard remain fixed during the event. Fractional footprint powers and logarithms use exact reals.

The volume is the smaller of the osmotic volume and the membrane's spherical cap. At equality the numerical law selects the slack branch. The empty or membraneless fallback has separate numerical cases.

numerical.result: On 169 directed pairs including 26 regime crossings, the maximum compiled CPU error was 1.07 × 10⁻¹⁴ kT compared with 1.70 × 10⁻¹⁰ on the earlier engine. Maximum disagreement around the eighteen four-event cycles was 5.33 × 10⁻¹⁵ kT.

biology.observable: Reversible osmotic work across a specified change in internal solute and membrane area, with a measured bath and starting and ending states.

claims.title: A short sum of logarithms prices ordered reaction draws
claims.statement: For a feasible number of ordered draws, summing one logarithm per draw gives the logarithm of the falling factorial. The engine's three-term mask therefore equals the log-factorial difference for every admitted reaction order.
assumptions: Counts and arities are natural numbers with 0 ≤ k ≤ 3 and k ≤ n. The exact-real sum excludes every inactive term. The numerical controls also exercise infeasible sides masked by the callers.
The isolated dilute reactant has unit concentration scale and encounter extent. The earlier catalog covers the additional membrane normalization and excess free energy.

numerical.result: Across 46 feasible count–arity pairs through 2²⁰ molecules, both backends and both direction kernels agreed with the log of the integer product to 3.55 × 10⁻¹⁵. All six infeasible pairs returned a masked direction. The earlier maximum log error was 1.20 × 10⁻⁹.

biology.observable: Counts and occupancy for a finite number of accessible reaction partners. Measured examples are recorded with the parent encounter claim.
biology.unit: Log of a dimensionless count product

claims.title: An inward membrane tube reduces the lumen inside a vesicle’s outer contour
claims.statement: Subtracting a nonnegative volume of bath-origin liquid inside an inward tube puts the lumen volume fraction at or below the outer-contour fraction. Geometry measured on the same vesicle can bound a fixed-area osmotic comparison.
assumptions: The initial vesicle has positive volume and no inward tube. At the endpoint the tube occupies a nonnegative volume within the outer contour. The upper bound is independent of its shape.

The numerical osmometer assumes initial osmotic balance at 66 mM, conserved internal solute and fixed area across the 72 mM challenge. The optional straight-cylinder estimate uses approximate reported dimensions.

numerical.result: A compiled 64-osmole world matched to the measured dimensionless loading predicts 4,125 µm³ at the specimen scale. The central outer-volume bound is 0.756 of the measured starting volume. A straight-cylinder estimate gives 0.705.

biology.observable: Volume and total membrane area of the same vesicle before and after an identified osmotic bath change, including the liquid inside its inward tube.
biology.unit: µm³ for volume and µm² for area

evidence.citation: Bhatia, Robinson and Dimova (2020), Soft Matter
evidence.locator: Figure 2, p. 7363. The Movie S1 caption in the publisher supplement, pp. 2–3, identifies the 66 to 72 mM transfer.
evidence.context: The same vesicle initially enclosed about 4,500 µm³. Its final outer contour enclosed 3,400.9 ± 1,000 µm³ and contained an inward tube about 18 µm long and 4 µm across.
evaluation: Outer volume as an upper bound on the final lumen
Straight circular tube as a stated geometric approximation
excluded: The separate Figure 4 transfer and its inferred internal concentration
evidence.uncertainty: The reported errors are about 25% for reconstructed area and 33% for volume. No statistical interpretation for the printed ± or independent tube-dimension errors is given.
evidence.assessment: The central tube-corrected lumen is about 950 µm³ below the 4,125 µm³ prediction. The reported outer-volume uncertainty alone spans that difference. The internal solute inventory was inferred.

claims.title: GARD v2 preserves the smaller catalyst on a reverse event within the precision bound
claims.statement: On a row’s integer grid, every signed update within the 106-bit bound produces the canonical high and low words for the new sum. Refolding the same counts recovers the same cache, and removing the moving molecule restores the parent’s rounded numerator.
assumptions: The catalyst coefficients are nonnegative multiples of each row’s least tick. The parser bounds the largest coefficient times the fission size to fewer than 2¹⁰⁶ ticks. Count products use at most 2²⁰ molecules and each coefficient part has at most 33 significant bits.

Rounding selects a nearest 53-bit word. TwoSum returns that rounded sum and its exact error. Hardware also needs finite intermediates and preservation of low words. The companion range comparison records the new guards and the earlier counterexamples.

numerical.result: The 2⁵⁴ stress event returned factors 2 and 2 and zero heat. All 22 signed updates matched the exact row and a fresh compiled fold. A 106-bit row passed and a 107-bit row was refused. The largest count was checked at the cache-function entry point. The repaired engine reproduced the complete earlier passing report byte for byte.

biology.observable: The underlying composition-dependent entry and exit rates can be measured. The numerical precision of the two-word representation is checked against exact arithmetic.
biology.unit: Dimensionless multiplier and kT per event

claims.title: GARD v2 guards the cache exponent range and honors explicit molecule capacity
claims.statement: The 106-bit width condition alone admits overflow. With the repaired upper and lower exponent guards, an exact intermediate of magnitude at most six times the row bound fits below the binary64 maximum, and any nonzero exact integer multiple of the row tick is at least one normal tick in magnitude. The parser resolves the tested explicit molecule capacities on either side of the default bucket limit.
assumptions: The row bound is its largest coefficient times the fission size. Lean assumes the six-times bound on an intermediate and integer-grid membership. It proves their arithmetic consequences. The original one-tick and overflow witnesses explain the extra guards.

The range replay uses a two-type world at fission size eight for the exponent cases. It exercises the parser, NumPy and the compiled CPU kernel. The explicit capacity cases use matched fission sizes of 4,096 and 4,097.

numerical.result: The repaired engine passed all nine cases. At size eight, 2¹⁰¹⁶ ran one event with a closed ledger. The upper boundary and two larger powers were refused. NumPy and compiled CPU preserved 2⁻¹⁰²², and the parser refused both inputs with subnormal low bits. Explicit capacities 4,096 and 4,097 resolved as requested. Six expectations differ on the earlier engine, where the original overflowing row stalled at a finite positive exact-reference rate.

biology.observable: The examples test numerical domain handling and parser reachability. No organism-specific catalyst range is assigned.
biology.unit: Binary exponent, row bits and molecule count

claims.title: Residue and energy accounts at producer replacement
claims.statement: When a departing occupant takes its unfinished chains and attached RNA and a newcomer starts with both empty, recording those exports preserves the residue account. With row and chain standard energies included, the endpoint energy account closes with zero heat assigned to the event. Successive differences of a cumulative counter recover its total change.
assumptions: A stage j complex holds j r residues, a completed product holds m r, and all extents update the same cumulative counters through the last step of the departing occupant.

Reconstruct incoming and outgoing rows’ mixing and standard energies from the exchanged amounts. Unfinished and attached residues leave at the chain’s standard energy per residue. Reading an individual generation requires both its counter endpoints.

numerical.result: All 65 current state fields matched byte for byte at four times after a disk checkpoint with occupied stages and hold, for both machine-return policies. The historical replay checked 40 fields. The [producer-labelled replacement replay](producer-replacement-rna.md) checks the departing material and producer identity. The full replacement-event residue and energy reconstruction remains open.

biology.observable: The template swap specifies which material leaves a simulated slot. Comparing it with biological inheritance would require a specified physical replacement process and measured outgoing and incoming material.

claims.title: Free and engaged polymerases or ribosomes sum to their machine pool
claims.statement: For chains sharing a machine pool, each update preserves free machines plus stage occupancies and the terminal holds that still engage a machine. A chain frees a machine at completion under the returned policy and at detachment under the held policy.
assumptions: The same signed extents update the stages, free machines and cumulative counters in each accepted half-step. Each chain has m ≥ 1 stages and length L = m r. Padded stages are inactive.
Each chain draws from one declared machine pool. All chains using that pool enter its balance, including chains already in progress.
Each chain’s policy stays fixed through the update. The same physical detachment extent leaves the terminal hold and frees its machine under the held policy.

numerical.result: Across 183 compiled observations the maximum pool residual was 5.80 × 10⁻¹⁹ fmol. Omitting one competing chain from the two-gene pool produced a 4.88 × 10⁻⁸ fmol discrepancy. On the neutral-label engine, 62 further observations across both terminal machine policies closed within 1.55 × 10⁻²⁰ fmol. Counting the initial hold under the opposite policy misplaced 80 machines in both cases.

biology.observable: Machine occupancy with a stated pool boundary, and separately measured RNA departure, polymerase persistence on DNA and new transcription.
biology.unit: Fractions of the stated experimental population, seconds for event timing and fmol of machines in Cells

evidence.locator: Figure 1e, Table 1 and supplementary Table S1.
evidence.context: At a common growth rate of 0.09 per hour, mRNA-bound E. coli ribosomes accounted for 31 ± 3%, 51 ± 3% and 65 ± 4% of the pool under carbon, nitrogen and phosphorus limitation, respectively.
evidence.uncertainty: Mean ± SEM across three biological replicates. Free subunits and free assembled ribosomes both enter the unbound pool. Bound particles can include stalled or initiating ribosomes.
evidence.assessment: The paired occupancy measurements establish condition dependence at matched growth. Both fractions share a denominator. An independent conservation test requires absolute counts and defined pool boundaries.

evidence.locator: Figures 1c–e and 3a,c and accompanying Results.
evidence.context: Purified E. coli polymerase remained at the DNA spot more than four seconds after sense RNA departure in 87 of 100 selected traces. A separate experiment detected antisense RNA in 78/114 traces with reverse motion and 5/257 without it.
evidence.uncertainty: The 100 traces came from two experiments. The four-second threshold reflects frame timing. The secondary transcription counts have separate motion-selected denominators.
evidence.assessment: These experiments distinguish RNA release, DNA retention and productive reuse. Return to a well-mixed free pool was unobserved.

claims.title: Stage exits account for residues in unfinished, terminally held and detached chains
claims.statement: Per chain, residues supplied at stage exits equal the increase in residues in unfinished chains and terminally held RNA plus the residues carried by physical detachments. The update allows nonempty initial stages and holds.
assumptions: The same signed extents update the stages, free machines and cumulative counters in each accepted half-step. Each chain has m ≥ 1 stages and length L = m r. Padded stages are inactive.

Stage j carries j r residues per occupied complex. Each completion moves L residues into a declared terminal hold. Each physical detachment moves L residues into its product fate. Cumulative detached RNA includes products subsequently degraded.

numerical.result: The largest residue residual across 183 observations was 3.39 × 10⁻²⁰ fmol. A one-stage chain retained zero residues in transit while releasing 6.55 × 10⁻⁵ fmol alongside an eight-stage chain. In the 62 neutral-label observations the combined stage, hold and detachment balance across both machine policies closed within 1.19 × 10⁻¹⁹ fmol.

biology.observable: Incorporated tracer partitioned between nascent chains and released protein in a matched preparation.
biology.unit: Counts per minute per unit of polysome OD₂₆₀ and seconds in the tracer study, fmol of residues in Cells

evidence.locator: Figure 4 and Table II, experiments 1–4.
evidence.context: The radiolabelled valine signals in soluble completed protein and polysome-associated nascent chains crossed at 34, 32, 40 and 32.5 s in four hamster-cell experiments.
evidence.uncertainty: Signals share a polysome optical-density normalization and include a correction for label attached outside nascent chains. The paper’s 23 ± 2 s transit time is a model-derived estimate.
evidence.assessment: The study resolves the two measured tracer pools. Relating its timing to the simulation requires matching the label pulse, precursor activity and sampling definitions.

claims.title: RNA keeps its producer label through export, cell replacement and return
claims.statement: For one producer label, combining the cell and outside-node balances cancels both directions of transport. Intracellular and extracellular degradation and the departure record each stay in the balance. The original producer’s stock in a new cell is at most cumulative gross return since replacement.
assumptions: Each gross transfer carries the share of its source. A cell replacement books all departing intracellular stock and leaves the extracellular pool and its labels in place.

The new cell starts with zero of the old producer label. Its only source of that label after replacement is reverse transport. Gross amount returned and all other outflows are nonnegative and the source share is at most one.
The earlier no-export specialization assumes one producer per fate row over its lifetime. Generation counters use their birth offsets. Normalized shares split the departed material across labels.

numerical.result: All 14 development-fixture checks passed on public Cells at fd2bb88c. The separate registered FR-38 comparison failed R1 and found R2 inconclusive (D313). The non-blind follow-up traced route 1 to gross cohort loss in the engine and net loss in the reference (D316). At the checkpoint, 1.0534 × 10⁻²⁶ fmol of founder RNA was inside the new cell after 1.1173 × 10⁻²⁶ fmol had returned. The combined durable RNA inventory closed within 6.01 × 10⁻²³ fmol. Exchanging two outside labels kept total RNA identical and misplaced 8.114 × 10⁻⁹ fmol. The reader detected it. The three standard retention outputs had finite bounds. Sparse-grid behavior is recorded separately.

biology.observable: Source-specific RNA measured before and after a change of producer, distinguishing removal from degradation and any RNA remaining outside the cell.
biology.unit: fmol or copy-equivalents by producer in Cells. Human plasma detection counts and donor miRNA copies per recipient cell in the studies.
biology.finding: Placental RNA can persist in plasma after delivery. In a separate cell preparation with donor cells absent, recipient cells genetically unable to produce the assayed RNA carried donor-derived molecules. The gross return rate across a cell replacement remains open.

evidence.locator: Figure 4C for two hours and Figure 4A for the separate 24-hour group, with the accompanying Results.
evidence.context: Paired maternal plasma samples at term, one before delivery and one afterwards. The two-hour group had a median 24,499 hPL mRNA copies/mL before delivery.
evidence.uncertainty: The Wilson 95% interval for the two-hour detection fraction, calculated from the published counts, is 12.7–57.6%. In the four detectable pairs, concentrations declined by approximately 66–97% from their own baselines.
evidence.assessment: At two hours 4 of 13 women had detectable hPL RNA. A separate group had 0 of 8 detectable at 24 hours. The assay measures a source-specific population signal. A quantitative comparison needs matched transfer and clearance measurements.

evidence.locator: Figures 3c–l and 4i. Figure 3l gives the copy count.
evidence.context: Native mouse miR-146a in recipient dendritic cell lysates 24 h after exposure to donor-derived extracellular vesicles. Donor cells were absent. Recipient cells lacked the assayed RNA gene. Vesicles from donor-null cells served as a control.
evidence.uncertainty: Three replicates, with SD plotted. The numerical SD was not extracted. The copy count may include RNA bound to the cell surface.
evidence.assessment: Recipients averaged about 370 donor copies per cell. A reporter supported functional intracellular access. The endpoint supports donor attribution and leaves the uptake rate and post-wash persistence unresolved.

claims.title: A retention estimate needs sampling during the export interval
claims.statement: Two equal positive pulses within an unsampled export interval give different retained amounts under positive first-order loss even when the cumulative export at both endpoints is identical.
assumptions: Constant positive first-order loss, positive pulse amount and the observation after both possible pulse times. The synthetic reader control uses the same cumulative export series up to replacement on both grids.

numerical.result: On 275b508f all 6 readouts on 3 grids matched their expected verdicts. Adding only post-replacement samples leaves the matching and mismatching outputs at insufficient resolution with a null bound. An interior export sample distinguishes the 1.707738-copy match from the 100-copy mismatch. The earlier frozen comparison records the false acceptance on fd2bb88c.

biology.observable: Time-resolved export throughout the founder’s lifetime and measured loss in the receiving pool.

claims.title: A lossless release fate gains all its detached RNA
claims.statement: For a fate row filled by a single release, amount gain equals cumulative detachment less loss. With established zero loss the gain equals the amount detached. The host comparison checks whether the exported fields let the cohort reader recover that surviving amount.
assumptions: One local release feeds the named row. The initial amount is known, the counters start at zero, and all changes to the row are included.
Zero cumulative loss must be established for that cell and fate. The public reader requires an explicit loss time series.

numerical.result: The original compiled comparison recorded three readable fates out of four. After the public exporter repair, the reader recovered all four in the two labelled worlds. Each row gained 1.27765623623 × 10⁻¹⁰ fmol over ten seconds, including 7.66593665955 × 10⁻¹¹ fmol marked during [2, 8) s. The largest physical balance residual was below 3.44 × 10⁻²⁷ fmol.

biology.observable: Absolute gain of a separately tracked RNA fate, with an independent count of its detachments and losses over the same interval.

claims.title: Resolving neutral labels can increase the heat booked for diffusion
