claims.statement: At a neutral Fick face, the sum of label powers exceeds or equals the parent power. Equality holds exactly when the label fractions agree at both ends. An accepted-step face booking with positive weights is zero exactly when every applied flux is zero.
assumptions: The two end concentrations, all normalized label fractions and the common mobility and temperature factor are strictly positive. The exact Cells face reduction uses its logarithmic quotient or equal-concentration branch on every row and the parent.

The timestep booking uses the applied mean flux and its predicted weight. The two-row square identity combines the two weights by addition. A separately simulated parent uses the weight predicted for its own concentration.
The trajectory comparison runs a closed, two-node neutral system with the same physical concentrations in both representations.

numerical.result: Across 800 accepted steps the largest reconstruction error was 3.68 × 10⁻¹⁶ pJ. Opposing labels booked 1.47315444 pJ in 1 s and the parent booked zero. With the same label fractions both booked 0.33000851 pJ.

biology.observable: Heat of mixing for independently characterized neutral tracers with equal mobility. Interpreting the extra booking for labels used solely to track provenance remains open.
biology.unit: pJ of heat over a specified interval

claims.title: A wash collects free tracer while surface-bound tracer can release later
claims.statement: A finite-volume wash collects the draw fraction of the free stock and preserves each bound stock at the event. At a previously equilibrated surface, dilution initiates net release. Free, bound, collected and supplied tracer satisfy one inventory through subsequent exchange.
assumptions: A well-mixed compartment is refilled to its original volume. Only free tracer is accessible to the instantaneous draw. The wall and specimen each hold a separately tracked bound stock.

For the strict release sign, the wash fraction, association rate and vacant site amount are positive, the buffer is more dilute than the free tracer, and the pre-wash surface is in binding equilibrium. The numerical well has unit binding multiplier and no internalisation.

numerical.result: Main’s stand-in and both FR-28 wall owners collected 30 fmol from 60 free. The wall held 10 fmol at the event and 9.97015402 fmol 10 ms later. Both candidate owners yielded identical traces. A matched buffer gave zero wall rate.

biology.observable: Tracer recovered in each wash and on the surface, with the time between dilution and measurement.
biology.unit: mass or fraction of initially adsorbed albumin, surface mass per area, fmol and fmol/s in Cells

evidence.citation: Robinson et al. (2014), Clinica Chimica Acta
evidence.locator: Supplementary Figure S3 and Tables S2 and S4, material 7.
evidence.context: The authors counted labelled albumin in six successive rinses and on the final disk. A separate pH 5 endpoint yielded 8.759 µg in pooled liquid and 22.96 ng/cm² on polyethylene terephthalate (0.22%, four replicates).
evidence.uncertainty: The rinse series has no per-rinse dwell time or error bars. The tabulated endpoint pools the starting sample, rinses and pipette tip and has no condition-specific uncertainty.
evidence.assessment: Independent recovery of tracer in liquid and on the surface is measured. The instantaneous bound fraction and the synthetic release constant remain open.

evidence.locator: Fig. 4 and Results §3.3, radiolabel distribution in one of three adsorption experiments.
evidence.context: Radiolabelled human serum albumin on expanded PTFE.
evidence.uncertainty: Bound fraction of adsorbed label after PBS rinses. Mass recovery exceeded 95% for the three trials. No uncertainty for these individual fractions, and substantial between-trial variation.
evidence.assessment: Three successive rinses removed part of the adsorbed albumin. At 10 and 30 mg/mL loading, 38.5% and 50.8% of adsorbed label remained after the third rinse.

evidence.locator: Fig. 2 and protein adsorption methods, uncoated graft controls, post-wash extracted human serum albumin.
evidence.context: Human serum albumin on uncoated expanded PTFE vascular grafts.
evidence.uncertainty: Uncoated ePTFE was water-washed before protein extraction and quantification. Reported mean and SD retain the paper’s units. The rinse effluent and pre-wash bound mass were unmeasured.
evidence.assessment: Extraction after washing recovered 1.47 ± 1.36 µg/m² (reported mean ± SD, seven specimens). The different wash media and measurements preclude a common rate.

pairs.assumption: Some albumin remains associated with uncoated expanded PTFE after a wash.
pairs.independence: Separate groups measured their own PTFE samples by radiotracing and protein extraction.
pairs.comparison: One study recovered 38.5–50.8% of adsorbed label on the surface after three rinses. The other recovered 1.47 ± 1.36 µg/m² from washed grafts. The shared result is positive residual surface stock.

replay.assessment: A full native draw retains all 10 fmol initially wall-bound in the control. Both laboratories detected a positive post-wash stock on ePTFE. The time-dependent release rate requires surface binding parameters and independently measured stock before and after rinsing.

biology.finding: Two independent laboratories recovered human serum albumin from washed expanded PTFE. Their measurements constrain the presence of a retained stock. A release rate requires comparable times and pre-wash bound amounts.

claims.title: Neutral label fluxes add and labels can exchange across a face with zero parent flux
claims.statement: For any finite partition of a neutral tracer, the sum of its label fluxes equals the parent flux under a common linear diffusion coefficient. With opposing 90:10 label fractions, a charged Cells face at fixed nonzero voltage instead gives a row sum (8/5)/ln(9) times the unsplit flux.
assumptions: Labels partition the material, share transport coefficients and experience the same voltage. Concentrations at both ends of each active logarithmic-mean face are positive and RT is positive.

The ideal Fick and neutral constant-field statements are exact over the reals. On the Cells face the exact neutral reduction uses equal concentrations or |(a−b)/(a+b)| ≥ 10⁻⁴ on every label and the parent. The small nonzero-gradient polynomial has a compiled comparison.
The charged example holds voltage fixed and changes only the representation of the tracer. Its ratio applies when the unsplit flux is nonzero.

numerical.result: Both nodes’ explicit labels summed to the parent at all 101 times. The right label reached 0.299998884 fmol at 1 s against 0.3 analytically. The compiled +1, +10 mV face gave a split-to-parent flux ratio of 0.7281913813014701.

biology.observable: Redistribution of a labelled molecular species, with matched diffusion coefficients and independently measured parent and label fluxes.
biology.unit: Relative fluorescence in the experiment and fmol in the simulation

evidence.locator: Figure 4A.
evidence.context: Photoactivated PSD-95 in one dendritic spine fell while green fluorescence increased in two nearby spines.
evidence.uncertainty: Green fluorescence was normalized to red fluorescence. The panel supplies no calibrated amount or common diffusion coefficient for the label and its complement.
evidence.assessment: Label redistribution is observed. Equal mobility, the parent flux and the charged-face ratio remain unmeasured in this preparation.

claims.title: A two-region sample represents the chamber under proportional withdrawal or equal concentrations
claims.statement: A finite draw has the chamber’s mean concentration exactly when the starting concentrations match or each region contributes the same fraction of its own volume. If region A is richer, drawing a larger fraction of A enriches the sample. Collected tracer and the dye left in each region account for the initial inventories and refill.
assumptions: There are two internally well-mixed regions of positive volume, and the total drawn volume is positive. Each local draw lies between zero and its available volume. A zero local draw has no event.

Each draw uses the pre-refill concentration, with no concurrent transport. The amount-above-background example uses a common background for the two initial regions and the refill. The local draw volumes and initial mixing are declared.

numerical.result: The three compiled 100 pL draws collected 8, 5 and 6.5 fmol above background. The corresponding regional remainders were (0, 2), (2.5, 2.5) and (2, 1.5) fmol within rounding. The compiled local inventories closed at all three recorded times in every case.

biology.observable: Collected dye and both post-draw regional amounts in a finite vessel with measured source concentrations and draw volumes.

evidence.citation: Johnson, Brown and Stockman (2006), Journal of Geophysical Research
evidence.locator: Methods paragraph 19 and continuous flow test 1, paragraph 33 and Figure 5a.
evidence.context: Equal rates of 1 g/L Rhodamine dye solution and distilled water fed a rough-walled glass fracture replica. The researchers measured each outlet flow and dye concentration.
evidence.uncertainty: The authors give rounded values for the half-flow case. Those values carry no reported concentration error bar.
evidence.assessment: At equal outlet flow the two branches measured about 75% and 25% of stock concentration. This supports enrichment in a physical flow system. The regional remainders after a finite draw remain unmeasured.

evidence.locator: Fig. 5, sequential bifurcations.
evidence.context: Dye and water at a 1:2 volume ratio in a droplet. Splits sampled an incompletely mixed dye gradient.
evidence.uncertainty: The figure gives daughter concentrations. The local volumes taken from different concentration regions and their remaining inventories are unknown.
evidence.assessment: The three labelled streams were at 70.8%, 61.1% and 55% of stock, all above the fully mixed 33⅓%.

evidence.locator: Figs. 5–6, two-stage device.
evidence.context: Bromophenol blue in injected and split droplets, with beads concentrated by a magnet and dissolved dye assayed by absorbance in pooled outlets.
evidence.uncertainty: Bulk outlet concentrations do not supply the source fractions drawn from each part of a droplet.
evidence.assessment: Collected dye measured 35.5 nM from 500 nM input, or 7.1%. This is a concentration measurement of the dissolved tracer.

pairs.assumption: A split from an incompletely mixed source can produce an outlet concentration different from the bulk mean.
pairs.independence: Independent fracture-replica and droplet experiments measured tracer in their own outlets.
pairs.comparison: At equal outlet flow, Johnson measured about 75% and 25% of stock for a 50% fully mixed reference. At successive bifurcations Tan measured 70.8%, 61.1% and 55% for a 33⅓% fully mixed reference.

replay.assessment: The existing compiled two-region draws reproduce enrichment with specified local concentrations and draw volumes. The experimental local draw fractions and both post-draw regional inventories remain unmeasured.

claims.title: Label remaining in a closed cell and clearance since the pulse account for the original cohort
claims.statement: After labelling stops, a solved tracer step changes the amount of old label in a region by labelled boundary inflow less local clearance. Across any finite sequence of such steps, label inside the region, label in the rest of the cell and clearance since the pulse sum to the amount present when the pulse ended.
assumptions: The nodes form one closed cell with a fixed region and recorded one-way internal routes. Any new material joins another cohort. Each accepted step solves the tracer’s stated linear equations and books clearance using the same cohort share.
The balance uses exact real arithmetic. Resolving the time course of mixing and inferring directional fluxes from two-way movement are separate questions.

numerical.result: The largest whole-cell residual was 5.20 × 10⁻¹⁸ fmol across 501 donor-cohort rows. Across 251 rows starting at the pulse switch it was 2.71 × 10⁻¹⁹ fmol. The pulse account subtracts the 5.327 × 10⁻⁵ fmol already cleared by that switch.

biology.observable: The same pre-labelled protein inside a defined region, in its full complement, and across the whole neuron over a chase, with clearance and export accounted for.
biology.unit: fmol in Cells and relative fluorescence in the imaged synapses

evidence.locator: Figure 6a–e and Supplementary Figure 9d.
evidence.context: A two-hour pulse/chase distinguished pre-existing and newly made PSD-95 in three mouse cortical pyramidal neurons.
evidence.uncertainty: The range 3,239–4,402 counts synaptic regions per neuron. It supplies no uncertainty on an old-label mass balance.
evidence.assessment: Endpoint maps show where old and new PSD-95 were detected. A longitudinal total including the diffuse pool is still needed to test the closed-cell balance.

claims.title: Identical donor traces under transfer and degradation have distinct receiver and loss records
claims.statement: Pure one-way transfer and local first-order degradation give the same donor curve for all times when their rate and starting amount agree. For a positive starting amount, rate and elapsed time, either receiver gain or cumulative clearance distinguishes the two mechanisms, and the two differences agree in magnitude.
assumptions: The two controls begin with identical donor and receiver amounts. Each has the same constant first-order rate, zero production, and a single route out of the donor. The transfer receiver retains all arriving label, and degradation books all removed label as loss.
The comparison uses amounts of the same cohort. A measured fluorescence ratio gives a local signal on a different scale.

numerical.result: The donors agreed exactly at all 11 outputs. At 0.5 s the transfer receiver gained 0.000393469 fmol with zero loss. Local degradation cleared 0.000393469 fmol with zero receiver gain.

biology.observable: Labelled protein at its source, at receiving synapses and across the cell, sampled over the same period.
biology.unit: fmol in Cells and per-spine green/red fluorescence ratio in the experiment

evidence.locator: Figure 4A.
evidence.context: After local photoactivation of PSD-95 in mouse neocortex, signal fell in the source spine and rose in two neighboring spines.
evidence.uncertainty: The figure reports relative fluorescence in selected spines. A recovered mass fraction and a same-cohort whole-neuron total are unavailable from those traces.
evidence.assessment: The receiver signals document local redistribution. The protein and cause of the 48-hour decline in the Cells study remain unresolved.

evidence.locator: Fig. 3b–d, endogenous Bassoon pulse and chase.
evidence.context: Fixed neuronal cultures labelled throughout. Soma and dendritic signal were compared across time points.
evidence.uncertainty: The regional mask omits much of the axon. The observations use sampled groups and lack a whole-cell balance.
evidence.assessment: Somatic Bassoon label decreased while dendrite-associated label increased. Dörrbaum Fig. 2C reuses these data.

evidence.locator: Fig. 5D,F.
evidence.context: Neuronal cultures with local photoactivation of tagged Bassoon at boutons.
evidence.uncertainty: The experiment does not measure surviving tagged Bassoon over the entire cell.
evidence.assessment: Label from a selectively activated region appeared at nearby unilluminated boutons. The regional increase is direct evidence for transfer.

pairs.assumption: Regional Bassoon measurements identify how much loss from a labelled source was transfer and how much was degradation.
pairs.independence: The tom Dieck and Tsuriel groups collected distinct data. The later Dörrbaum replot of the tom Dieck images is the same dataset.
pairs.comparison: One assay shows somatic label falling as dendrite-associated signal rises. Local photoactivation in the other directly shows labelled Bassoon arriving at neighbouring boutons.

replay.assessment: Cells can book source loss and recipient gain. A quantitative decomposition needs the surviving label in the rest of the same cell, including unobserved axons.

claims.title: Matched-buffer heat per molecule tends to zero when sampling follows the liquid volume fraction
claims.statement: When the buffer supplies exactly the fraction f of the starting count at each place, the mixing heat of every split lies between zero and its physical split score. For one nonempty place with n molecules and sampler probability q=f, the mean heat is positive and at most the entropy of the withdrawn count, hence at most ln(n+1) in k_BT. The mean per starting molecule tends to zero along increasing, exactly matched pool sizes.
assumptions: The finite pool has the additive discrete ideal free energy. All counts are nonnegative integers and 0 < f < 1. Exact matching requires b = nf for every place being compared.

The mean uses one independent uniform midpoint word per original molecule. The volume fraction and its finite-word probability must agree for the entropy bound, including the tested quarters, halves, eighths and three-quarters.
The limit concerns a fixed fraction and a sequence of admissible pool sizes tending to infinity. The finite bound applies at every positive size with an exactly matched integer buffer.

numerical.result: All 42,875 exact count comparisons passed. Across seven parsed pools and 575 guarded outcomes, the largest heat error against an 88-digit reference was 1.13 × 10⁻¹² k_BT. In a quarter wash the mean heat per starting molecule was 0.024193 k_BT at n=100 and 0.007775 k_BT at n=400. A complete three-species wash booked 4.535007 k_BT of heat against a split score of 5.164075.

biology.observable: Mean energy dissipated per starting tracer molecule in a partial exchange, with measured volumes and counts and concentration-matched buffer, across a range of pool sizes.

claims.title: Partial withdrawal closes the energy balance and releases nonnegative mixing heat
claims.statement: For every count split and supplied buffer, the change of pool free energy equals buffer work minus pool loss minus mixing heat. The loss equals sample free energy minus the physical binomial split score. Both the split score and the mixing heat are nonnegative. For a tracer-free buffer the mean heat per initial tracer is −(1−q) ln(1−f), where q is the effective withdrawal probability and f is the physical volume fraction.
assumptions: The pool has finitely many places with nonnegative integer counts. Its discrete ideal free energy is additive over finite species and includes the log factorial of each count. The buffer fills the withdrawn volume and the full pool volume is restored.
The physical fraction f lies strictly between zero and one. Work, sink and heat use Cells’ withdrawal convention in units of k_BT. Closure and signs hold for each realized split.

Sampler probabilities and mean heats assume independent, uniformly distributed word indices. Cells compares each midpoint from 2⁵² bins strictly to f. The split-score comparison uses outcomes with positive sampler probability.

numerical.result: Three complete worlds and 1,080 small-count cases matched an 88-digit independent reference. The largest balance error was 6.21 × 10⁻¹⁴ k_BT. All booked heats were nonnegative. At f = 1−2⁻⁵³ the last word retains one tracer, the split score exceeds its sampler score by ln 2, and the word-weighted tracer-free mean is 8.1572 × 10⁻¹⁵ k_BT against an ideal-volume mean of 4.0786 × 10⁻¹⁵ k_BT.

biology.observable: Independent energy budget for a measured partial withdrawal with known tracer counts, buffer content, liquid volumes and work during resupply.

claims.title: Partial pool withdrawal conserves counts and fixes their conditional moments
claims.statement: For a well-mixed pool place, the molecules left in the pool plus those withdrawn equal the original count plus the supplied buffer after the wash. For n original molecules sampled independently with probability q, the withdrawn mean is nq, its variance is nq(1−q), and the final pool has mean n(1−q)+buffer with the same variance.
assumptions: Initial and supplied counts are nonnegative integers and their sum fits the place capacity. The count balance holds for every per-molecule assignment.

The moment calculation averages independent, equiprobable word indices for the molecules. The actual stream uses the midpoints of M = 2^52 bins and withdraws when the midpoint is strictly less than f. PRNG independence is a modeling assumption.

The effective probability q equals ceil(Mf−1/2)/M for 0 ≤ f ≤ 1. The error is bounded by 2⁻⁵³, including at midpoint ties. For transfer at the measured liquid fraction, the tracer must sample that liquid uniformly.

numerical.result: All finite places balanced in three complete population runs. With eight molecules, 4,000 seeds per fraction gave means 1.993, 3.991 and 2.6405 at one quarter, one half and one third. Sample variances were 1.479, 1.997 and 1.738. Nine controls at or around word cutoffs matched the exact finite-grid law. At f = 2⁻⁵³ the parser admits the wash and every molecule stays.

biology.observable: Fraction of passive tracer beads in a sampled or retained daughter at an independently estimated liquid fraction.

evidence.locator: Passive center daughter, Figure 2c, all 180 vector markers.
evidence.context: Ten-micrometre polystyrene beads in droplets split into approximately equal thirds. The center is the sampled branch.
evidence.uncertainty: The center volume was nominal. Per-droplet daughter volumes and a sampling criterion for bead-free droplets were unreported.
evidence.assessment: The nominal geometry underpredicts the mean of the 180 bead fractions by 0.117. At nine parent beads the sample mean was 4.0 versus 3.0 predicted, while the sample variance was 2.18 versus 2.00 beads². Unequal volumes and advection remain possible.

evidence.locator: Side-channel withdrawal at 4.5 µL/min, Figure 4b–c, acoustics off.
evidence.context: A separate droplet chip removes side streams and retains the center. The liquid retention estimate uses the center and input volumes at the same flow.
evidence.uncertainty: The center volume was 12.8 ± 1.1 nL, with the parent about 47 nL from the figure. Volume averages used 50 droplets. Bead retention had SD 0.044 across 20 splits.
evidence.assessment: Passive bead and volume retention are close in this preparation. Individual volumes paired with bead counts would distinguish independent sampling from geometry-dependent sorting.

evidence.locator: Fig. 6d, field-off control showing the parent and two separated daughter droplets.
evidence.context: A magnet-off split in a separate microfluidic droplet device.
evidence.uncertainty: No per-split volume calibration, count table or replicated passive occupancy fraction. The adjacent 59% withdrawal estimate was obtained during magnetic retention and is excluded.
evidence.assessment: Particles occupied both daughters in the illustrated passive split. The published quantitative withdrawal volume belongs to magnetic retention.

pairs.assumption: On average the retained passive bead fraction equals the actual retained liquid fraction.
pairs.independence: The chip experiments are distinct. Anna Fornell and Maria Tenje participated in both studies.
pairs.comparison: Fornell’s mean across 180 split fractions is 0.450 versus a nominal liquid fraction of ⅓. Liu measured 0.282 ± 0.044 bead retention (20 splits), with a separate volume pool giving 12.8/47 ≈ 0.272 (50 measurements). No individual liquid fraction is linked to a parent/daughter count.

replay.assessment: At nominal f = ⅓ Cells gives three beads for a nine-bead parent on average. Fornell observed four. Liu’s independently estimated group liquid fraction is 0.272 versus 0.282 bead retention. Missing per-droplet liquid fractions and shared investigators preclude a replicated mean or variance discrepancy.

pairs.assumption: One passive split can leave beads in both the withdrawn and retained liquid.
pairs.independence: The Fornell group and the Sahore group acquired their own images using different devices.
pairs.comparison: Fornell’s passive scatter includes points strictly between zero and the total parent count. Sahore’s magnet-off example directly shows beads in both daughters. The second study supplies no frequency of that event.

replay.assessment: Native withdrawal can draw and retain a positive number of particles in the same event. Both devices show this possibility. The independent image supplies no probability, liquid fraction or per-droplet denominator.

biology.finding: Two separate laboratories observed both daughters retaining particles in a passive split. The two quantitative studies share investigators and lack per-event liquid fractions. Independent mean and variance tests remain open.

claims.title: A finite-pool wash preserves assembly cargo and books the two bath energies
claims.statement: A replacement swaps the finite bath at one isolated stop. For each finite species, the inventory after the stop plus the removed bath equals the inventory before plus the supplied bath. A tracer-free wash leaves exactly the tracer retained by the slots available for later exchange. When bath and slot energies are additive, the change in total free energy equals fresh-bath work minus the spent-bath sink.
assumptions: Each slot survives the stop. The pool volume is fixed and fresh finite counts fit the execution capacity. The signed energy calculation uses the same units and standard potentials on both sides.

Between the wash and later observations, the tracer can move between bath and slots. Binding inside a slot preserves its tracer moiety. The history assumes no tracer source, sink, lysis or further wash.

numerical.result: In the two-vesicle CPU world a pulse supplied 12 tracer molecules. The wash removed six and retained six, including three bound to membrane sites. Tracer inventory closed exactly at all 856 saved rows. All six nonzero material edges matched the independently reconstructed receipts, and the maximum bath or world energy discrepancy was below 2.85 × 10⁻¹⁴ kBT. After washing at 2 s, release preceded uptake at 2.000848 s and 2.001470 s. The 21 November pulse-and-wash replay preserved the tracer ledger on all 856 rows with a maximum energy discrepancy of 2.85 × 10⁻¹⁴ kBT.

biology.observable: External tracer depletion, cargo retained by surviving vesicles, and redistribution to finite recipient membranes.
biology.unit: fluorescence units, fraction of total fluorescence, and elapsed time
biology.finding: Giant vesicles retained fluorescent cargo after external label fell to near background. A separate liposome experiment measured transfer between finite donor and recipient membranes. The synthetic fixture’s return time and absolute retention remain uncalibrated.

evidence.citation: Zhao et al., supporting Figure S3a–c
evidence.locator: Supporting Figure S3a–c and solution-exchange methods.
evidence.context: Trapped giant unilamellar vesicles containing fluorescent dextran. The replacement liquid contained the unlabelled polymers.
evidence.uncertainty: Three preparations, 3–4 measurements per position, error bars SD. Some vesicles were lost and no per-vesicle retained fraction was reported.
evidence.assessment: After 40 min of flow at 1 µL/min the exterior signal was approximately 0.1 fluorescence units while surviving vesicles retained fluorescent contents.

evidence.locator: Figure 7A and adjacent text on C6-NBD-PC exchange.
evidence.context: DOPC-based donor and acceptor liposomes. Acceptor material was twice the donor amount.
evidence.uncertainty: The figure shows a representative trace from three experiments. The crossover has no reported uncertainty interval.
evidence.assessment: The signal reached about 48% of total fluorescence at 3.8 min. The assay resolves redistribution between populations. It does not identify a molecule returning to its original vesicle.

claims.title: A fresh bath one molecule beyond capacity loses a logarithmic term if accepted
claims.statement: For a dilute species with count M + 1, using the last log-factorial entry M in its discrete ideal energy understates that energy by ln(M + 1) kBT. The molecular capacity must cover every finite count committed by an accepted replacement or serial transfer.
assumptions: M is a positive integer capacity. The discrete ideal energy consists of a linear term in the full molecular count and a log-factorial term. At the first count outside the table the lookup returns the entry at M.
The test replaces the bath at the horizon. The fresh bath is below the osmotic ceiling, and the transfer keeps both living slots.

numerical.result: Both schedules now reject 33 molecules at capacity 32 during definition. Both accepted 32 at 32 and 33 at 64 with the reference work. The earlier comparison records the incorrect work of an accepted oversized pool.

biology.observable: The table limit is an implementation property. Its reference is the discrete ideal free energy of the finite bath.

claims.title: Magnesium shifts the apparent equilibrium of adenylate kinase
claims.statement: One signed extent of 2 ADP ⇌ ATP + AMP conserves adenylates, phosphate groups and Mg-free base-form charge. At free Mg concentration m, the total-nucleotide equilibrium quotient equals K_base (1 + m/a)/(1 + m/d)². For d ≥ 2a it reaches its maximum at m = d − 2a.
assumptions: ATP and ADP each bind one Mg with positive dissociation constants a and d in the same units as m. AMP remains free. The enabled reaction reads positive free nucleotide activities and includes the ATP binding factor in its kinetic prefactor.
The quotient is [ATP]_total [AMP]/[ADP]_total². The equilibrium formula extends to zero Mg by continuity. The engine's log-activity evaluator uses positive inputs.

numerical.result: Across 21 Mg and nucleotide loads, the largest flux discrepancy was 7.04 × 10⁻¹⁵ of the forward rate. The three nucleotide changes followed their signed extents in two tissue steps. With the declared binding constants the predicted maximum is 1.5104 at 0.299 mM free Mg. At the 3.809 mM buffer match, omitting the Mg prefactor reduced the nonzero flux by a factor of 159.69.

pairs.assumption: The apparent adenylate-kinase equilibrium quotient formed from total nucleotides depends on free Mg²⁺.
pairs.independence: Lawson and Veech measured a myokinase preparation. Kleczkowski and Randall measured their own purified maize-leaf enzyme.
pairs.comparison: The first assay gave 0.391 at zero free Mg²⁺ and 1.05 at 1 mM. The maize assay reported a span of 0.30–1.27 across 0.0014–8.3 mM and 0.76 ± 0.10 at 1.8–1.9 mM. Both resolve dependence on Mg²⁺. They leave the position of the Cells maximum and its transfer to heart mitochondria open.

replay.assessment: The calculated quotient rises from 0.389 in the zero-Mg limit to 1.101 at 1 mM in the first assay. The second assay’s 1.8–1.9 mM interval gives 0.744–0.772. The peak location and tissue transfer remain open.

biology.observable: Total-nucleotide equilibrium quotient as a function of free Mg in a defined preparation.
biology.unit: dimensionless quotient and mM free Mg
biology.finding: Two enzyme assays support a magnesium-dependent equilibrium. The position of the predicted maximum and its transfer to the cardiac intermembrane space remain open.

evidence.locator: Abstract, myokinase equilibrium on total nucleotides at 0 and 1 mM free Mg.
evidence.context: pH 7.0, 38 °C, ionic strength 0.25 M. Cells uses its declared 25 °C constants.
evidence.uncertainty: The abstract gives neither pointwise uncertainties nor the method for establishing zero free Mg.
evidence.assessment: The measured quotient rose from 0.391 to 1.05. The model gives 0.3890 in the zero-Mg limit and 1.1013 at 1 mM.

evidence.locator: Abstract, apparent equilibrium at 1.8–1.9 mM free Mg.
evidence.context: Purified maize-leaf adenylate kinase.
evidence.uncertainty: The authors report ±0.10. The abstract does not specify the type of uncertainty.
evidence.assessment: The reported quotient was 0.76 ± 0.10. Cells gives 0.744–0.772 over the reported free-Mg range.

claims.title: The held reductant supply has a pH-dependent stall and balances work in either direction
claims.statement: The enabled supply stalls exactly when free matrix NADH/NAD equals the held reduced-to-oxidized donor ratio times the reference proton concentration divided by the free matrix proton concentration. At any signed flux, work supplied by the held pair equals the dissipated heat plus chemical work delivered to NAD, NADH and H⁺.
assumptions: The matrix reaction is S_red + NAD ⇌ S_ox + NADH + H⁺. Both donor rows are held. The reaction has no charge transfer across the membrane.
Free activities and the kinetic prefactor are positive. Cells assigns zero standard drive at its reference proton concentration of 10⁻⁷ M. Work and heat refer to instantaneous chemical power.

numerical.result: Across 24 pH, phosphate and NADH loads the largest net-flux discrepancy was 1.23 × 10⁻¹⁴ of the forward rate. For a held ratio of 3.63858 the stalled NADH/NAD ratio was 4.5807 at pH 7.1 and 9.1397 at pH 7.4. The two-step tissue run kept the donor amounts fixed, recorded opposite donor receipts and moved NAD and NADH with opposite signs. Held work matched heat plus delivered chemical work within a relative tolerance of 2 × 10⁻¹² at positive and negative flux.

biology.observable: Dependence of the free NADH/NAD equilibrium ratio on proton activity and the reduced-to-oxidized donor ratio. The absolute stall and heat require a specified donor.
biology.unit: dimensionless activity ratio, M for the measured equilibrium quotient, pJ/s for the model heat
biology.finding: A named ketone-body donor exhibits the one-proton equilibrium dependence. The absolute stall ratio and heat for the Cells donor remain unmeasured.

evidence.locator: Table 3, equilibrium of D-β-hydroxybutyrate dehydrogenase.
evidence.context: The β-hydroxybutyrate/acetoacetate donor pair at 38 °C, ionic strength 0.255 M and pH 6.84–7.16.
evidence.uncertainty: SEM of 25 determinations.
evidence.assessment: The quotient [acetoacetate][NADH][H⁺]/([β-hydroxybutyrate][NAD⁺]) was (4.94 ± 0.086) × 10⁻⁹ M. This measures the proton dependence and equilibrium for this specific donor pair.

claims.title: Mitochondrial cycles reverse at zero free energy and dissipate power in either direction
claims.statement: Each enabled mitochondrial cycle runs forward at negative full-turn ΔG, reverses at positive ΔG and stalls at zero. The five electrogenic cycles have a stall voltage set by free activities. Phosphate uptake and K⁺/H⁺ exchange have voltage-independent stall ratios. At positive temperature, instantaneous dissipated power is positive in either direction and vanishes exactly at stall or when the population is off.
assumptions: Each reaction uses the declared free species and signed charge, with N the matrix and P the intermembrane space. Free activities are positive. The dimensionless voltage is F(φ_N − φ_P)/(RT).
An enabled population has a positive finite forward kinetic prefactor. Complex III uses a half-turn exponent and complex IV a quarter-turn exponent. ΔG refers to a full turnover in both cases.
Heat here is the model's instantaneous chemical free-energy dissipation. Flux is in fmol/s and RT in J/mol. An assay of integrated whole-mitochondrion enthalpy measures a different observable.

numerical.result: All 49 physical settings agreed with the independent component equations on NumPy and compiled CPU JAX, including both sides of stall for all seven laws. The worst net-flux error was 3.91 × 10⁻¹⁴ of the reference forward rate. The worst residual ΔG/(RT) at a calculated stall was 2.85 × 10⁻¹⁴. The rate kernel also preserved the signs at ±2⁻⁶⁰ and returned zero at an exact zero input. The probe and the stage agreed on flux and instantaneous dissipated power.

biology.observable: Net turnover on either side of a measured mitochondrial stall, the shift in ATP synthase stall with phosphorylation load, and dissipated power at known cycle affinity.
biology.unit: turnovers per enzyme per second, pH units, H⁺/ATP, pJ/s per population

evidence.citation: Petersen et al. (2012), Figs. 1–4 and Tables S2 and S4
evidence.locator: Yeast traces in Fig. 1, corrected stall in Fig. 2, fitted coupling in Fig. 4 and all ten corrected stall entries in Table S4.
evidence.context: Purified yeast mitochondrial ATP synthase in proteoliposomes at an imposed 60 mV.
evidence.uncertainty: The example rates are fitted initial slopes. The equilibrium ΔpH was interpolated. One measured stall sets the offset for comparing shifts at the other loads. The comparison adds the reported interpolation limits and assumes the assay's concentration quotient is proportional to the free activity quotient.
evidence.assessment: ATP turnover changed sign across stall, and the inferred coupling was 2.9 ± 0.2 H⁺/ATP. The model's three protons predict a 0.745 pH-unit endpoint shift against 0.74 observed. Five of nine other entries are within the combined interpolation limits using the stall at Q = 5.79 as the reference. Four intermediate entries fall outside.

evidence.locator: The anaerobic bulk heat pulse in Fig. 5b and its dependence on the initial ADP in Fig. 6.
evidence.context: Rat liver mitochondria following aerobic ATP production and oxygen exhaustion.
evidence.uncertainty: The apparent enthalpy was −29 ± 7 kJ per mole of previously added ADP. The authors inferred an ATP hydrolysis contribution.
evidence.assessment: Bulk calorimetry integrates heat from the preparation. The instantaneous dissipated power of each individual mitochondrial cycle remains experimentally open.

claims.title: Restoring both respiratory carriers fixes the turnover ratio and outward charge
claims.statement: For signed extents of mitochondrial complexes I, III and IV, restoring reduced quinone and reduced cytochrome c fixes their turnover in the ratio 2:2:1. Two NADH and one oxygen then give twenty outward charge equivalents, with every intermediate redox carrier restored.
assumptions: N is the matrix and P the intermembrane space. The tracked species use the registered base forms, with explicit protons. Water is implicit.
The complete-chain ratio assumes no other source or sink for the two intermediate carriers. The per-cycle identities hold for arbitrary signed extents, including a transient.

numerical.result: All seven registered columns were checked against independently written material balances. Per forward turnover the respiratory complexes added 4, 2 and 8 net charges on P, while each added four explicit P protons. In two checked steps of a finite-matrix/lumen world, the redox, adenine and phosphate changes matched predictions from the measured extents within 8.28 × 10⁻²⁵ fmol.

pairs.assumption: Forward bovine complex I translocates about four protons per pair of electrons.
pairs.independence: The Moscow and Cambridge groups prepared their own bovine heart submitochondrial particles and used different assays.
pairs.comparison: Galkin measured 4.00 ± 0.05 H⁺/2e⁻ from proton and NADH rates. Jones obtained 4.21 ± 0.15, 4.10 ± 0.17 and 4.02 ± 0.19 from three flux comparisons on the same four preparations. This constrains complex I. The complete three-complex charge cycle remains unmeasured here.

replay.assessment: The native material column posts four protons per two electrons on the P side. This ratio is independent of rate and matches the shared stoichiometric observable. The preparations do not measure the full respiratory chain in this comparison.

biology.observable: Protons transported per NADH, including correction for proton consumption by quinone reduction, and net charge transport during a carrier-balanced respiratory sequence.
biology.unit: H⁺ per NADH or two electrons, charge equivalents per O₂

evidence.citation: Galkin et al. (1999), Fig. 2 and Eq. 3
evidence.locator: Fig. 2, right panel, and the scalar-proton correction in Eq. 3.
evidence.context: NADH-driven quinone reduction in inside-out bovine heart submitochondrial particles.
evidence.uncertainty: The authors report 4.00 ± 0.05, estimated from initial rates after correcting for one proton consumed by quinone reduction.
evidence.assessment: The observed 4.00 ± 0.05 transported protons per two electrons agrees with the four on P per forward complex I turnover. The full three-complex charge balance needs additional measurements.

evidence.citation: Jones et al. (2017), Table 3 and Fig. 3
evidence.locator: Bovine estimates in Table 3 derived from the paired flux measurements in Fig. 3.
evidence.context: Four bovine heart submitochondrial preparations. The three comparisons match ATP synthesis rates to approximate equal proton leak.
evidence.uncertainty: Reported propagated errors. All three comparisons use the same four preparations.
evidence.assessment: The estimates were 4.21 ± 0.15, 4.10 ± 0.17 and 4.02 ± 0.19 H⁺/2e⁻. They support a value near four for complex I. They do not directly measure the three-complex net charge.

claims.title: ATP synthesis and delivery return four charge equivalents in the declared three-proton model
claims.statement: One ATP synthesis, nucleotide exchange and phosphate import restore the matrix ATP, ADP and phosphate rows and deliver one ATP on P. Their net P-side charge is −4. Potassium–proton exchange swaps one K for one H with zero net charge. At balanced respiratory carriers and zero net charge transfer the seven paths imply five ATP deliveries per oxygen.
assumptions: The registered synthase has three translocated protons per matrix ATP. Nucleotides and phosphate use the declared base forms and all proton rows are explicit.
The five-per-O₂ identity assumes matched turnovers of synthesis, ATP export and phosphate import, and no additional electrogenic paths. It is an ideal stoichiometric ratio.

numerical.result: The synthesized ATP, nucleotide exchange, phosphate import and K/H exchange carry −3, −1, 0 and 0 net charge equivalents on P per turn. All seven populations carried nonzero extents in two checked 1 ms steps. The independently calculated combined material postings matched the engine ledger. Global charge error stayed below 1.0 × 10⁻³³ C.

biology.observable: Rotor proton count and ATP turnover for synthesis, plus the energetic cost of delivering ATP across the mitochondrial inner membrane.
biology.unit: c-subunits per rotor, H⁺ per matrix ATP, charge equivalents per delivered ATP

pairs.assumption: Exactly three protons per ATP is the intrinsic tight-coupling ratio of the mammalian mitochondrial ATP synthases represented by the Cells model.
pairs.independence: The sheep particles and cryo-EM density are new. The initial reconstruction and atomic fit used bovine 5ARA, which itself used Watt’s 2XND. Independence of the eight-subunit count from the starting model is unconfirmed.
pairs.comparison: Both structures contain eight c-subunits. One proton per c-subunit and three ATP per turn imply 8/3 H⁺ per synthesized ATP, compared with 3 in Cells. The distinction concerns ideal rotor coupling. Effective proton cost under load or during ATP export requires flux measurements.

replay.assessment: The two density datasets share a model-template lineage. Cells posts three protons per ATP for this leg. A rotor count constrains ideal coupling, and a paired flux is needed to assess effective cost under load.

evidence.citation: Pinke et al. (2020), ovine cryo-EM structure 6TT7
evidence.locator: State 1a, deposited EM map EMD-10573 and PDB 6TT7, entities 2 and 10.
evidence.context: ATP synthase purified from sheep heart mitochondria, imaged by cryo-EM.
evidence.uncertainty: Subunit counts are structural observations. One H⁺ per c-subunit and three ATP per turn are the tight-coupling interpretation. There is no simultaneous H⁺ and ATP flux measurement.
evidence.assessment: The ovine assembly has eight c-subunits and three catalytic β-subunits. Its new density corroborates the 8/3 tight-coupling interpretation, with a shared bovine starting model for the rotor. The delivered ATP cost also depends on the export and phosphate paths.

evidence.citation: Watt et al. (2010), Fig. 1 and Discussion
evidence.locator: The bovine c-ring in Fig. 1 and the authors' coupling interpretation.
evidence.context: Structure of the bovine mitochondrial F1–c-ring complex.
evidence.uncertainty: The 3.5 Å structure resolves eight c-subunits. The stoichiometric interpretation assumes tight coupling and three ATP per full rotation.
evidence.assessment: The bovine structure implies 8/3 H⁺ per matrix ATP under tight coupling, and the authors infer 11/3 proton equivalents per delivered ATP. The current Cells model fixes 3 and 4. The structural result identifies a preparation-specific limit of that choice. It does not measure ATP flux under load.

claims.title: Each compartment belongs to one cell and its charge sets its lumen voltage
claims.statement: Summing each cell's cytosol with the compartments it owns counts every species amount once. A lumen with a single bounding capacitor sits above its owner's potential by its net free charge divided by that capacitance.
assumptions: Each finite lumen has exactly one owner and positive bounding capacitance. The voltage formula assumes that its bounding membrane supplies its only capacitor plate.
In the numerical comparison each cell and lumen exchange material externally only with their own held bath.

numerical.result: Two cells and their private lumens balanced every species against the corresponding bath within 4.34 × 10⁻¹⁹ fmol. The trafficking lumen reached +29.83 mV relative to its owner at the end of retrieval. The largest discrepancy from charge divided by capacitance across both lumens was 1.39 × 10⁻¹⁷ V.

biology.observable: Lumen voltage relative to its own cytosol, with whole-compartment free charge and capacitance in the same preparation.

evidence.locator: Resting lysosome measurements in Fig. 4i and the optical calibration in Fig. 4.
evidence.context: Intact HEK293 cells. The experimental convention is lumen minus cytosol. The Cells bounding patch uses the opposite orientation.
evidence.uncertainty: Mean ± SD across seven independent experiments with 106 lysosome regions. The calibration estimates its zero-potential endpoint.
evidence.assessment: Resting lumen potential was +56 ± 7 mV relative to cytosol. This locates the resting voltage in this preparation. The experiment supplies neither net free charge nor capacitance, and the checked generic lumen has no calibrated native transport.

claims.title: Returning membrane area can leave some of its channels in the receiving pool
claims.statement: Retrieval carries away source-specific capacitance and leaves each population proportional to the remaining area fraction raised to its enrichment. Transfers conserve area, capacitance and each channel population. Returning the same area from a seeded, uniformly mixed pool leaves a positive share of the retrieved cohort inside.
assumptions: A positive source area remains after each transfer. Enrichments are nonnegative, constant over the compared stages and refer to the population at its source patch.
The round-trip formula uses uniform retrieval and recycling for the tracked cohort, a positive seed area, no initial internal cohort and no production or removal during the cycle.

numerical.result: A four-step cycle recovered all retrieved area. Of the initial 3,261.27 Kir units, 444.72 (13.64%) stayed in the pool. Two populations followed independent enrichment and recycling predictions within 3.42 × 10⁻¹³ units. The plasma gained 2.224 pF from mixing with a pool of higher specific capacitance. A separate extreme depletion comparison is recorded under empty-surface-flow.

biology.observable: Time-resolved membrane area or capacitance, internal cargo, and surface cargo of the same cohort during retrieval and recycling.
biology.unit: pF and fraction of labelled cargo

evidence.locator: Fig. 5c–d for the snapshot and Fig. 5e for recycling in a separate chase.
evidence.context: Endogenous AMPA receptors in basal primary hippocampal neuronal cultures. The snapshot uses whole-cell label. The chase uses a reference surface signal.
evidence.uncertainty: Mean ± SEM, three biological replicates for each measurement.
evidence.assessment: After 10 h of labelling, 90.4 ± 0.6% of the label was at the surface and 10.3 ± 1.7% was internal. In the 15 min chase, resurfaced label was 12.5 ± 2.8% of the reference surface signal. The missing terminal internal stock prevents a closed recycling balance.

evidence.locator: Fig. 1C–E, peak capacitance and the fractions of capacitance and synaptotagmin-2 fluorescence remaining 60 s after stimulation.
evidence.context: Stimulated calyces of Held in brainstem slices at room temperature. Each readout is normalized to its own peak excess.
evidence.uncertainty: Mean ± SEM across seven capacitance and ten fluorescence recordings. Seven were simultaneous. Fluorescence depends on vesicle re-acidification.
evidence.assessment: After a 1.52 ± 0.21 pF capacitance rise, 0.33 ± 0.06 of peak excess capacitance and 0.47 ± 0.07 of peak fluorescence remained at 60 s. These measurements constrain net retrieval and cargo recovery separately. Absolute internal channel counts remain open.

evidence.locator: Figure 7A–B and Results, days 1 and 4 after transient receptor block
evidence.context: Adult mouse sternomastoid endplates. Repeat surface labelling distinguishes previously exposed receptors that resurfaced from newly inserted receptors.
evidence.uncertainty: Four-day values and SDs from Results. The graph shows SEM. The denominator is the initial surface fluorescence. The study did not measure the final size of the internal receptor pool or the area of membrane returned.
evidence.assessment: At four days, resurfaced receptors contributed 26 ± 5% of the original surface fluorescence and newly inserted receptors 24 ± 5% (SD, 29 junctions). The original and recycled tags were distinguished experimentally.

biology.finding: Independent neuronal AMPA and muscle nicotinic receptor preparations both detected previously exposed receptors returning to the surface. Neither closes the full membrane-area and receptor-pool balance.

pairs.assumption: Some previously surface-exposed neurotransmitter receptors return to the membrane after internalization.
pairs.independence: Ojima’s group followed endogenous AMPA receptors in cultured hippocampal neurons. Bruneau’s group independently tracked nicotinic receptors at living mouse neuromuscular junctions.
pairs.comparison: Ojima found resurfaced label equal to 12.5 ± 2.8% of reference surface signal after 15 min (SEM, three biological replicates). Bruneau found 26 ± 5% of initial surface signal after four days (SD, 29 junctions). The return is replicated. Different denominators, cargo and times prevent a common recycling-rate estimate, and terminal internal stocks were unmeasured.

replay.assessment: A native two-population recycling cycle returns retrieved units. Each study observed some resurfacing. Neither supplies the terminal internal stock and returned membrane area for its own quantitative balance.

claims.title: Charge carriers reconcile daughter volume and membrane shares at division
claims.statement: Each species balances across the daughters when charge carriers compensate for the difference between volume-weighted and area-weighted parent charge. Splitting each capacitor and its charge in the same proportion preserves patch voltage. Positive daughter amounts have nonnegative ideal unmixing cost.
assumptions: Volume and active patch shares lie strictly between zero and one. Capacitors are positive. Compensating carrier charge fractions sum to one and each carrier has nonzero valence.
Both daughters have positive amounts and proportional reference volumes. The independent work calculation uses the single-parent fixture with one membrane against a held bath.

numerical.result: For a 75% volume share and a 60% membrane share, K and counterion offsets of +0.001008 and −0.001008 fmol supplied the 1.94515 × 10⁻¹³ C mismatch. At the event, each daughter pair summed to the parent's amount exactly in float64. Daughter voltages agreed with the parent's within 1.39 × 10⁻¹⁷ V. Booked work agreed with a 65-digit unmixing calculation within 1.69 × 10⁻¹⁷ pJ.

biology.observable: Parent and both daughter volumes, ionic amounts, patch areas and potentials immediately across division.

evidence.locator: Supplement p. 4, panel labelled S2L and cited as S2L in the main text.
evidence.context: Eleven paired mouse basal epidermal divisions in vivo. The next image after the mitotic parent gives the sum of both daughters.
evidence.uncertainty: The imaging interval was 12 h. Mean repeat-segmentation difference across the study was 9.1 ± 8.6%.
evidence.assessment: The mean parent volume was 770 µm³ and the mean summed daughter volume in the next image was 677 µm³. The interval includes growth and mitotic volume changes. Instantaneous volume, carrier charge and voltage partition remain open.

claims.title: A closing daughter bridge scales flux by its remaining aperture
claims.statement: Successive intervals compose for capped linear and exponential aperture closure. Linear closure reaches zero at its declared deadline. Exponential closure stays positive at every finite time from a positive starting aperture. The remaining aperture scales the fully open bridge's permeability–area product.
assumptions: Closure is continuously enabled over the tested intervals, with a positive initial aperture and a fixed positive closure time.

The flux comparison evaluates the same concentrations, potentials and gate before and after changing only bridge availability. The single-stalk biological comparison assumes proportionality between stalk diameter and aperture.

numerical.result: After the checked division, both eight-step worlds matched the corresponding analytic aperture. At the 3 ms deadline availability was 0 for linear closure and 0.367879 for exponential closure. Species fluxes agreed with the same-state open flux scaled by analytic aperture within 5.09 × 10⁻²¹ fmol/s.

biology.observable: Bridge diameter and inter-daughter transport during late cytokinesis in the same bridge, including the time and conditions of isolation.
biology.unit: µm, s, nS, normalized tracer exchange per second

evidence.locator: Fig. 1D, microtubule-stalk diameter at the midbody rim in one representative bridge. Fig. 1E relates microtubule loss to membrane closure.
evidence.context: Developing zebrafish embryos. The first plotted frame sets elapsed time. Diameter ratios equal aperture ratios under the proxy assumption.
evidence.uncertainty: The plotted series has no pointwise error bars. The overall series comprised 18 bridges in five embryos. Membrane continuity can outlast tubulin visibility.
evidence.assessment: The held-out diameter at 15 min was about 1.6 µm. The first two readings predicted 0 µm for linear closure and 0.655 µm for exponential closure. Both miss the plateau in this bridge. Actual ionic aperture and variability among bridges remain open.

evidence.locator: Original measurements in section 5. Fig. 2A shows the midbody and 2C reports the conductance distribution.
evidence.context: Dividing sister-cell pairs from a human cell line with a visible midbody bridge. Conductance was measured across the two daughters.
evidence.uncertainty: Fifteen bridges, with a reported mean of 32 ± 6 nS. The authors do not identify the error statistic. Elapsed time in Fig. 2B follows a recording, and bridge age since furrowing was unreported.
evidence.assessment: Conductance ranged from below 1 to 70 nS. This supplies an electrical scale. The study lacks simultaneous repeated radii for testing conductance as a function of aperture.

evidence.locator: Fig. 4D–E, control dextran exchange slopes, with time measured from furrow ingression.
evidence.context: First division of C. elegans embryos. The observable is 10 kDa dextran exchange normalized by the initial inter-daughter fluorescence difference.
evidence.uncertainty: Approximate graph readings with 90% intervals, about ten slopes per bin and partially overlapping windows.
evidence.assessment: The exchange slope fell from 0.0108/s (0.0085–0.0130) at 30 s to −0.0004/s (−0.0019–0.0011) at 260 s. The late interval includes zero. This establishes loss of measurable tracer exchange without fixing the ionic conductance or its time law.

claims.title: Precursor molecules balance across maturation, surface insertion and removal
claims.statement: Routes on the same precursor and cell share first-order consumption. Weighting each route's functional units by its precursor stoichiometry accounts for molecules in transit, on the surface and in the removal ledger. A two-stage maturation pulse and a surface cohort undergoing first-order loss have explicit time courses.
assumptions: Rates are constant over each interval. Each route has a positive number of precursor molecules per functional unit. Unit amounts evolve continuously. The material identity admits any finite number of sequential maturation pools, including direct insertion.
The pulse starts entirely in the first of two identical stages with no new input or surface removal. The cohort survival comparison tracks labelled surface units with no new labelled insertions.

numerical.result: An eight-step checked world used two precursor molecules per direct unit and seven per three-stage unit. All observed precursor, transit, insertion, surface and sink amounts matched the independent matrix exponential within 4.55 × 10⁻¹³ units and 4.24 × 10⁻²² fmol. In a compiled two-stage pulse, 10.82448 of the initial 120 units reached the membrane in 12.5 ms. Two declared populations reproduce each of the two published fast/slow receptor fits.

biology.observable: Survival of a labelled surface-channel cohort and appearance of newly made receptors in the plasma membrane.
biology.unit: % of labelled baseline and hours to surface appearance

evidence.locator: Filled circles in Figure 3D, anchored to day 7. Elapsed times and percent retention were read from the point centers and caps.
evidence.context: Ten innervated mouse hindlimbs were followed with the other leg denervated. Residual receptor-associated label is a proxy for survival. The day-7 normalization favors the slower component.
fit: Anchor and seven elapsed days (100% and approximately 67%)
evidence.uncertainty: Readings are approximate. The caption specifies SD and the methods specify SEM. Repeated measures share the animals and baseline.
evidence.assessment: A single rate of 0.05721/day predicted 44.89%, 40.04% and 35.71% retention against 48%, 43% and 42%. The first two predictions fall inside the plotted bars. The last lies below the observed 39–46% bar.

evidence.locator: Abstract observations over the first 3 and 3.5 hours.
evidence.context: Newly synthesized acetylcholine receptors were followed to the plasma membrane in cultured chick skeletal muscle.
evidence.uncertainty: The observations describe relative labelling of receptors arriving at the membrane. The report gives no numerical fraction or error for the 3.5-hour observation.
evidence.assessment: Few labelled receptors reached the surface during the first three hours. By 3.5 hours virtually all receptors entering the membrane carried label. This supports a lag in appearance and leaves the pool count and transit-time distribution open.

evidence.citation: Bruneau and Akaaboune (2010), Results and Fig. 3D
evidence.locator: Results, pp. 616–617 and Fig. 3D
evidence.context: Active adult mouse sternomastoid synapses. Fewer than 20% of AChRs labelled, muscle fibers expressing rapsyn–GFP.
evidence.uncertainty: Values and times from Results (SD). The figure caption specifies SEM for the plotted bars. Two follow-ups cannot identify the decay law.
evidence.assessment: The labelled fraction remaining was 93 ± 5% at 24 h and 75 ± 8% at 72 h. These observations constrain the direction of loss in an active synapse.

evidence.locator: Table 2, innervated adult mouse muscles, fitted components
evidence.context: Labelled AChR in innervated tibialis anterior. The two-component fit is normalized at day 2. The pre-existing claim's Fig. 3D uses a day-7 anchor in the same study.
evidence.uncertainty: Table 2 means and SD for ten muscles. These fitted components and the Fig. 3 observations have common provenance.
evidence.assessment: In innervated muscles, the authors fitted a 13 ± 2% fast component with half-life 1.1 ± 0.3 days and an 87 ± 2% slow component with half-life 13.1 ± 0.4 days.

evidence.locator: Primary report, Science 222, 67–69, abstract with component estimates
evidence.context: Normally innervated mouse diaphragm neuromuscular junctions.
evidence.uncertainty: Published component estimates. The public abstract gives no pointwise time series, errors or sample counts. The inferred subpopulation fractions are approximate.
evidence.assessment: The authors reported a fast fraction of approximately 20% with an 18.7 h half-life and a slow component with a 12.4 day half-life. Each component is a fit to a subpopulation.

biology.finding: Independent labelled cohorts decline over time. Two innervated mouse preparations resolved fast and slow receptor populations. A common loss constant across the entire pool would miss that heterogeneity. The precursor and removal inventories remain open.

pairs.assumption: A labelled surface acetylcholine-receptor cohort declines over time at an active, innervated adult mouse neuromuscular junction.
pairs.independence: Strack’s group followed hindlimb muscle. Bruneau and Akaaboune independently followed sternomastoid synapses with less than 20% of receptors labelled.
pairs.comparison: Strack’s labelled signal fell to approximately 67% seven days after its day-7 anchor. The sternomastoid series retained 93 ± 5% at 24 h and 75 ± 8% at 72 h (SD, five synapses each). Both support loss of the detectable cohort. Different anchors and labelling protocols preclude transfer of one fitted rate.

replay.assessment: Strack’s single-rate fit gives decreasing signal at the later observations. Bruneau’s two measurements also decrease. The second preparation has no independently supplied loss rate or intermediate cohort measurement for a held-out decay curve.

pairs.assumption: All labelled junctional acetylcholine receptors in a normally innervated mouse muscle share one first-order loss rate.
pairs.independence: The hindlimb and diaphragm curves were collected by different laboratories. Strack’s Table 2 fit and day-7 observations are from the same publication.
pairs.comparison: Strack fitted 1.1 ± 0.3 and 13.1 ± 0.4 day half-lives (SD, ten muscles). Stanley and Drachman reported 18.7 hours and 12.4 days. Fast fractions were about 13% and 20%, respectively. Both support a mixture of lifetimes. A separately tracked cohort can still have first-order loss.

replay.assessment: Two declared populations with each study’s own fractions and half-lives reproduce both fitted decay components. Seven days after their respective fit origins, the compiled summed fractions are 0.602 and 0.541. The input fits determine these outputs.

claims.title: At fixed channel drive, whole-patch flow tracks the surface unit count
claims.statement: The membrane state converts declared abundance and a signed unit change to a density at the current patch area. Multiplication by area cancels that dilution, so total channel flow scales with the surface unit count at fixed single-channel drive.
assumptions: Patch area and reference density are positive. Capacitance, voltage, concentration difference, permeability and gating are fixed for the flow comparison.
The endplate comparison assumes that available binding-site density is proportional to available functional units across conditions, with comparable effective areas and per-unit driving conditions.

numerical.result: At 1, 1.4 and 1.8 times the declared area, two populations on one patch preserved their potassium fluxes at fixed count. Halving each count halved its flux. The largest relative difference was 4.45 × 10⁻¹⁶ across NumPy and compiled CPU controls.

biology.observable: Peak synaptic-current magnitude at measured available receptor-site densities and whole-patch flow at fixed count as surface area changes.

evidence.locator: Table 1 reports available receptor-site densities and absolute miniature endplate current amplitudes for three conditions.
evidence.context: Esterase-inactivated lizard intercostal endplates were recorded at −100 mV and 23 °C. Density is per µm² of receptor-rich membrane.
fit: Control with 18,000 sites/µm² and 7.5 nA mean peak current
evidence.uncertainty: Estimated standard errors include systematic uncertainties in current and density. The table gives condition means without a biological sample count per row.
evidence.assessment: Scaling by central density gave 3.42 and 2.88 nA against 4.0 ± 0.7 and 2.5 ± 0.5 nA. Both values are within the reported current uncertainties. The measurements leave the functional unit count and the effect of varying area at fixed count open.

evidence.citation: Ohno et al. (2002), Table 2, patient 3 and controls
evidence.locator: Table 2 and footnotes. Patient 3 and controls for the adult comparison
evidence.context: Human intercostal endplates. A receptor-scaffold deficiency reduced available binding sites. Miniature endplate currents were recorded at −80 mV and 22 ± 0.5 °C.
evidence.uncertainty: Table reports SE. No error or replicate count for this patient’s binding-site estimate. The measurements were not linked by individual endplate. Endplate geometry, local opening and transmitter exposure could differ. Patient 4 was a child and has no age-matched site count in the table.
evidence.assessment: The adult patient had 5.7 million binding sites per endplate and a 1.83 ± 0.15 nA mean current. Controls had 12.82 ± 0.79 million sites and 3.95 ± 0.10 nA. The patient retained 44.5% of the adult mean sites and 46.3% of control current.

biology.finding: Two preparations link a smaller receptor binding-site count or density to a smaller miniature endplate current. Exact proportionality at fixed unit drive and the effect of changing area at fixed count remain open.

pairs.assumption: Within each preparation, fewer available postsynaptic acetylcholine-receptor binding sites accompany a smaller miniature endplate current.
pairs.independence: Land’s group compared experimentally reduced site density at lizard endplates. Ohno’s group assayed human intercostal muscle with a receptor-scaffold deficiency.
pairs.comparison: In lizard muscle, available sites fell from 18,000 to 8,200 and 6,900 per µm² as mean peak currents fell from 7.5 to 4.0 and 2.5 nA. In the adult human comparison, sites and current retained 44.5% and 46.3% of control. Current and binding measurements lack matching by individual human endplate. Geometry, occupancy and transmitter exposure limit a test of exact proportionality.

replay.assessment: With fixed opening and drive, halving native counts halves current. Scaling by the lizard site measurements gives 3.42 and 2.88 nA. The human site ratio gives 44.5% against a current ratio of 46.3%. Endplate-specific opening, stimulus and paired site counts are unavailable.

claims.title: An empty surface population has zero abundance and channel flow
claims.statement: Removing the full declared number of functional units sets both the normalized abundance and the channel's contribution to zero for any positive patch area. The original two-term float64 readout retained a signed residue at certain areas.
assumptions: The two initial channel counts are exactly representable, and the state subtracts those counts exactly. The engine accepts the controlled state at each tested area.

The controlled states isolate abundance at fixed capacitance and drive. A second comparison follows a scheduled four-step retrieval from the declared initial state of 3,072 Kir units, with synthetic enrichment 1,024 and a total area decrease of 30%.

numerical.result: Six prepared states at three area ratios on NumPy and JAX CPU gave exact zeros for abundance and potassium flux. The retrieval rollout completed and every zero-count observation through 4 ms had exactly zero abundance and flux.

biology.observable: The zero-unit case is a numerical identity. Resolving a physiological consequence would require a measurable residual current.

claims.title: Simultaneous replacement books the old and arriving species, charge and electrical work
claims.statement: At each due site the previous occupant leaves and a template or a copy of a pre-event donor enters. Gross supply minus gross removal equals the tissue change for each species. Valence weights give the signed charge. The equal shares of field energy less electrode work sum to one field adjustment.
assumptions: A finite set of tissue sites is replaced simultaneously. Sites outside that set retain their amounts. Copying a donor uses its pre-event amounts, including when that donor is also due.

Field-energy sharing requires at least one due site. Capacitor energy and held-electrode work enter the formal result as signed inputs. The numerical comparison computes each independently for a sheet with one membrane and one held bath per cell.

numerical.result: One cell copied a donor that simultaneously received a template. Gross species transfers, image charge, electrode work and generation replay matched the expected state. The largest per-site free-energy residual was 2.21 × 10⁻¹³ pJ against 2 × 10⁻¹¹ pJ. A three-step checked sheet recorded exactly one exchange at each of the two due sites. D264 separately holds the exported reaction rate at the replacement time.

biology.observable: Time between basal-layer exit and compensating local division, and the species amounts in the departing and arriving cells at one site.

evidence.locator: Figure 3C follows neighboring fates after a basal cell differentiates.
evidence.context: Intravital recordings covered two 90 × 90 µm fields of adult mouse epidermis and counted 524 divisions and 529 differentiations.
evidence.uncertainty: The main panel shows one mouse. The 1.8-day estimate is a fitted coordination time scale.
evidence.assessment: Neighboring division followed differentiation on a 1.8-day time scale. Cells takes its schedule as an input. The assay leaves the identity and ion inventory of an immediate same-site arrival open.

claims.title: Replacement over water accounts for incoming volume and composition-dependent free energy
claims.statement: For a donor copy, transfer of the donor's volume increment preserves its physical volume when reference volumes agree. Adding the water term to the chemical energy at the declared volume evaluates all tracked species at the physical volume. A composition change can give nonzero water free energy even at zero net volume transfer.
assumptions: All cell volumes and the reference volume are positive. The finite-species ideal chemical identity assumes positive amounts. Each site keeps its own elastic pressure law and fixed extra impermeant amount.
The donor and receiver have the same declared water compartment and initial reference volume. Species amounts and physical volume are read at the two endpoints of the event.

numerical.result: The copy stayed at 0.788048 pL, gained 1.1003 fmol of tracked osmoles and booked −0.138369 pJ of water free energy. The template changed both amount and volume at the other site. The largest combined energy discrepancy was 4.32 × 10⁻¹³ pJ against 2 × 10⁻¹¹ pJ. A three-step checked run reproduced both gross volume bookings.

biology.observable: Paired volume before removal and after arrival at the same site, with intracellular osmoles and mechanical or osmotic work.
biology.unit: pL per cell, µm³ per division, % of baseline volume and pJ per event

evidence.locator: Supplement page 4, panel marked S2L. Eleven line segments pair the mitotic parent with both daughters at the next frame.
evidence.context: Mouse basal epidermal cells were followed in vivo at 12-hour intervals. The register stores the paired figure readings in µm³.
evidence.uncertainty: The paired changes had a sample SD of 100 µm³. The authors report 9.1 ± 8.6% repeat-segmentation error overall. Imaging spans a full frame interval.
evidence.assessment: Mean volume was 770 µm³ for each parent and 677 µm³ for the sum of its daughters, with nine of eleven pairs decreasing. The paired change averaged −94 µm³. This measures division and leaves the same-site replacement volume and work open.

evidence.locator: Figure 1l and the accompanying results give the change in GFP-derived cytoplasmic volume.
evidence.context: MDCKII epithelial monolayers experienced a 20% hypertonic shock. Cells were grouped by subsequent extrusion or retention.
evidence.uncertainty: Values are mean ± SEM. The caption reports n = 5.
evidence.assessment: Cells subsequently extruded lost 20 ± 3% of baseline volume and retained cells lost 11 ± 2.5%. The assay measures outgoing shrinkage. Incoming absolute volume, osmole counts and work remain open.

claims.title: Centering a strictly interior replacement volume preserves its water-domain membership in exact arithmetic
claims.statement: For any declared target strictly between the water bounds, subtracting and adding the same reference volume recovers that target. The numerical comparison tests how v2 binds a target whose float64 offset would reconstruct at the excluded lower bound.
assumptions: The water volume interval is open at both endpoints. The exact theorem uses a common real-valued reference for storing and reconstructing the target.
The admission comparison uses a single template with the slot's own species amounts. Water flow is disabled and all other inputs are held fixed.

numerical.result: The repaired v2 definition admitted 0.18763056296676509 pL, the first float above the strict lower bound of 0.18763056296676506 pL. It also admitted the second interior float and refused the bound itself. The binding regression verified that the adjusted offset reconstructs strictly inside. The earlier comparison records the original refusal.

biology.observable: Cell volume and measurement uncertainty near a physiologically justified lower bound. The boundary replay tests numerical admission.

claims.title: Size-triggered fission conserves each species under fixed-quota and independent partitions
claims.statement: Single-molecule growth and conservative division at the threshold cannot overshoot it. Ranking all occupied places selects exactly the declared quota. For a tracer species, fixed-quota sampling and independent per-molecule assignment give different probabilities of a tracer-free daughter, even when their mean allocations agree.
assumptions: Each molecule occupies one place and belongs to one species. The second daughter receives the complement. A split acts at the threshold before further growth.

The rank proof applies to any realized stable ordering and integer quota. The equal-subset probability assumes equiprobable rankings. The engine floors the float64 product of the fraction and the parent size.

For the binomial probabilities each molecule independently enters the named daughter with the same probability p. Comparing a center branch to two pooled side branches also assumes p is represented by the center volume fraction.

numerical.result: For a parent with two marked and two unmarked molecules, the named daughter had zero markers in 4 of 24 fixed-half rankings and 4 of 16 independent fair assignments. Padded places, ties and adjacent float64 quotas matched the specification. Exact weighted enumeration at parent counts 7, 9 and 12 matched the binomial variances at p = 1/3.

biology.observable: Variance of the center daughter's marked-particle count across divisions with a fixed reconstructed total.

evidence.locator: Figure 2c on printed page 031101-3. The pale-blue series gives the ultrasound-off control. Both side outlets are pooled.
evidence.context: Water droplets containing polystyrene beads split into three daughters of approximately equal volume. All 180 plotted control splits contribute to the empty-center comparison. The sample variances use reconstructed totals of 7, 9 and 12 beads.
evidence.uncertainty: At nine beads there are twelve plotted splits. The seven- and twelve-bead groups each contain seven splits. Counts were read from vector markers, including overlapping markers. Per-split volume fractions and raw paired counts are unavailable in the cited figure.
evidence.assessment: At nine beads the measured sample variance was 2.18, compared with 2.00 under independent assignment. At seven and twelve beads the measured values were 0.95 and 4.48, compared with 1.56 and 2.67. The 180 splits had zero empty centers. The nominal volume model gives a 26% probability of that outcome if splits are independent. The data leave independence and the engine’s size trigger unresolved.

claims.title: Switching an empty daughter pick to its sibling changes the sampled lineage
claims.statement: For a positive parent, the fallback always retains a nonempty daughter. When one daughter is empty, a fair initial pick retains the whole parent under fallback and half the parent on average if the initial pick stands. For either choice, the followed daughter’s log-weight jump equals minus the split work plus its sibling’s outgoing free energy.
assumptions: The initial choice and the partition are separate. The selection average gives each daughter label equal probability, then applies the declared empty-daughter policy.
An empty assembly has zero total molecules. A tracer-free daughter can still contain other species. Counts are measured at birth, before further chemical events.
A daughter at the size threshold divides again if its fission limit allows it. The signed work and sink use the assembly’s log weight with zero log weight for the empty state.

numerical.result: Across 32 equiprobable partition-and-pick outcomes for four molecules, fallback raised mean retained size from 2.00 to 2.25. At quota zero, selecting an empty daughter ended a lineage and following the full sibling gave five immediate re-splits before the limit. The every-descendant run recorded four empty and four full daughter births. The signed energy bookings matched the reference within 3.11 × 10⁻¹⁵ k_BT. The ledger docstring has a sign typo in its derivation.

biology.observable: Birth sizes and subsequent fates of both daughters, with the rule used to select the tracked daughter recorded for empty as well as occupied outcomes.
biology.finding: The bead experiment in the partition claim measures the cargo of a liquid droplet. Its center-versus-pooled-sides readout cannot identify an empty assembly or which sibling was followed. A direct measurement of this selection effect remains open.

claims.title: Vesicle pore rates scale with area and increase on warming
claims.statement: At fixed temperature and tension, the rate of first pore opening is area times a common per-area rate. At fixed area and tension, the logarithmic sensitivity to temperature exceeds 5/2 everywhere the Phase A hold is admitted. Warming between two admitted temperatures therefore increases the rate.
assumptions: The area, tension σ, absolute temperature T, line tension Γ, prefactor and activation energy E_A are positive. The material parameters are fixed as temperature changes. The SI rate uses E_A/R and the tension scale πΓ²/k_B.
