evidence.assessment: Both ion gradients were needed for excess ATP labelling, which ouabain prevented. This measures isotope incorporation. Independent ATP pool-size changes would be needed for net synthesis.

evidence.locator: Reverse-pump current in dialysed squid axons, pp. 450–452.
evidence.context: Voltage-clamped squid giant axons under reverse-favouring pump conditions.
evidence.uncertainty: An inward current identifies direction. An absolute sign-change voltage requires a fixed-chemistry crossing.
evidence.assessment: The squid preparation directly resolved inward current when the Na/K pump ran backward.

evidence.locator: Fig. 5 and pp. 611–612.
evidence.context: Sheep cardiac Purkinje cells with Cs as the K substitute, at a fixed ionic recipe in each voltage sweep.
evidence.uncertainty: Five cells per curve. At about −39 kJ/mol the currents between −95 and −20 mV could not be distinguished from zero.
evidence.assessment: Currents were significantly inward below −95 mV and outward above −20 mV. The authors’ approximate −60 mV and calculated −24 mV both lie in the unresolved interval.

pairs.assumption: Opposing Na and K gradients increase ouabain-sensitive radiophosphate incorporation into ATP in red-cell ghosts.
pairs.independence: Garrahan and Glynn and Lant and Whittam each prepared and assayed their own ghosts.
pairs.comparison: Both groups saw ATP labelling increase with a K-rich interior and Na-rich, nominally K-free exterior. Ouabain reduced the excess. Background nucleotide labelling remained. Exchange can produce the signal without net ATP synthesis.

replay.assessment: The pump readout is signed net cycle flux. Both experiments measure isotope entering ATP. Without tracer-specific gross forward and reverse fluxes and background exchange, the two quantities cannot be compared, even at zero net flux.

pairs.assumption: The Na/K pump can carry inward electrical current under reverse-favouring conditions in voltage-clamped excitable cells.
pairs.independence: Separate squid and sheep laboratories used original recordings. The sheep experiment substituted Cs for K.
pairs.comparison: Pump-specific inward current was observed in squid axons and in sheep cardiac cells. In the cardiac series at about −39 kJ/mol the sign was resolved below −95 mV and above −20 mV.

replay.assessment: The enabled native pump runs backward below its calculated stall. The broad cardiac zero interval includes both −60 and −24 mV. A quantitative transfer requires the Cs protocol and matched activities. The red-cell isotope assay addresses a different observable.

claims.title: Extracellular face flux follows the electrochemical potential drop
claims.statement: Reversing the endpoints and voltage reverses the signed flux. A positive face coefficient gives positive flux exactly when the sender’s electrochemical potential is higher. At equilibrium the flux is zero, including when the concentration and electrical drives cancel.
assumptions: Both endpoint concentrations and RT are positive. The two orientations use the same ion, temperature, geometry and diffusivity.
The proof evaluates the two log-ratio branches and the fourth-degree small-gradient mean in exact real arithmetic. The force uses the difference of the endpoint logs.

numerical.result: Opposing voltage reversed a resolved concentration-driven flux. At zero voltage, 100.00000000000001 and 100 mM gave zero CPU flux versus 1.42 × 10⁻¹⁸ fmol/s in the scalar reference. The absolute tolerance was 3 × 10⁻¹² fmol/s. Across 60 tissue flux observations, the largest absolute discrepancy was 1.50 × 10⁻¹⁷ fmol/s.

biology.observable: Species-resolved ion transfer rate between two extracellular compartments, with measured concentrations at both endpoints and their voltage difference.
biology.finding: Diluting NaCl on opposite sides of a claudin-2 pore shifted its current-reversal voltage in opposite directions. Reversal of an individual ion’s net flux remains unmeasured. [Weber et al., Fig. 6A–B](https://elifesciences.org/articles/09906)

claims.title: Passive extracellular face transport dissipates energy
claims.statement: Each ion’s signed flux multiplied by its electrochemical potential drop is nonnegative. Summing the contributions over all ions gives nonnegative instantaneous face power.
assumptions: Endpoint concentrations and RT are positive. Each ion has a nonnegative face coefficient. Power is evaluated at a single state.

numerical.result: Face power agreed with the scalar reference across eleven CPU cases. Reversing a resolved flux and its endpoint bookings preserved the total material rate and gave −4.52 × 10⁻⁵ pJ/s, failing the direction and power checks.

biology.observable: Instantaneous energy loss inferred from species-resolved fluxes and measured electrochemical potential differences across an extracellular interface.
biology.finding: Trout gill epithelia supplied two-way sodium tracer flux and voltage measurements. Active transport contributed to the measured flux, so passive heat production cannot be inferred from these data alone. [Galvez et al., Fig. 3 and Tables 1–2](https://www.zoology.ubc.ca/~woodcm/Woodblog/wp-content/uploads/2016/07/Galvez-et-al.-2008-In-Vitro-Cell.pdf)

claims.title: A moving binder carries its ligands across a face
claims.statement: Each binder form contributes one binder and its signed ligand stoichiometry to every transfer. The stored rows conserve their inventories across the endpoints and recover the movers’ charge. Ligand can cross even at zero net binder flux.
assumptions: Each face credits and debits the same signed transfer. The inventory statement sums the face contributions on a finite closed network. Any reservoir, reaction or membrane contribution to an observed node needs its own accounting.

Counts are integers relative to the reference form. For the zero-net-binder case, the two forms have swapped positive endpoint concentrations, the same positive diffusivity and zero voltage difference. The ligand carried by the occupied form moves in addition to any independent free-ligand flux.

numerical.result: Across four compiled CPU tissue steps, both nodes matched the independently reconstructed binder and H⁺ transfers within 6.94 × 10⁻¹⁸ fmol. Two kernel controls moved ligand at zero net binder flux. Omitting a signed ligand count preserved global totals but missed the shared node by 12 or 6 fmol/s.

biology.observable: Simultaneous transfers of free ligand, individual binder forms and total binder between compartments with measured geometry and endpoint concentrations.
biology.finding: Carbonic buffer shortened acid arrival between regions of a rabbit heart cell. Mobile myoglobin increased initial oxygen flux in a polymer film. Both support facilitated transport. Passage of each binding form across the same interface remains unmeasured.
biology.unit: fmol per stored row in Cells, s for acid arrival and kg O₂ m⁻² h⁻¹ for oxygen flux

evidence.locator: Figures 1–2 and the Results on diffusion delay.
evidence.context: Isolated rabbit ventricular myocytes at 36 °C. The readout was a 20 nM rise in free intracellular H⁺ at sites about 40 µm apart.
evidence.uncertainty: Arrival delay was 25.1 ± 5.1 s in HEPES (10 cells), 5.93 ± 2.96 s with carbonic buffer (7 cells) and 15.53 ± 2.65 s with carbonic anhydrase inhibited (8 cells). Errors are SEM across separate groups.
evidence.assessment: Buffer chemistry and its kinetics affected acid transport. Predicting these times requires spatial geometry and reaction rates. The effective diffusion coefficients were inferred from the same delays.

evidence.locator: Figures 6–7.
evidence.context: Dissolved oxygen crossed a polymer film with or without horse myoglobin at 25 °C.
evidence.uncertainty: The carrier-free film gave 3 × 10⁻⁷ kg m⁻² h⁻¹. Initial flux with uncrosslinked myoglobin was about threefold higher. Tests were in triplicate and the authors reported deviation below 10% without specifying its definition.
evidence.assessment: Myoglobin later leached out. Crosslinking also impaired oxygen unloading, so the controls leave the effect of mobility alone unresolved.

claims.title: Edge orientation preserves each compartment’s transfer balance
claims.statement: Reversing any subset of edge orientations and their signed fluxes preserves each compartment’s credit or debit.
assumptions: Every transfer is booked once at its sender and once at its receiver. The edge set is finite and multiple edges may share a compartment.

numerical.result: The per-cell comparison passed for the declared owners. Swapping owners alone preserved the global total and produced a per-cell discrepancy of 2.40 × 10⁻⁴ fmol/s.

biology.observable: Net ion gain or loss in each of two identified compartments over the same transfer interval.
biology.finding: Paired clamp recordings showed equal and opposite junctional currents. Calibrated gain and loss of the same ion in both cells remain unmeasured. [Wang and Veenstra, Fig. 1A and C](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9101407/)

claims.title: Only boundary transfers change a region’s inventory during transport
claims.statement: Internal edges cancel when transfers are summed over a region. On the entire closed graph each species and any charge-weighted sum are conserved.
assumptions: Each edge transfers equal amounts between its two endpoints. A held bath needs an external supply term when included in an inventory.

numerical.result: The closed tissue run checked the potassium ledger, including membrane, pump and channel contributions. The chain comparison exercised both entering and leaving transfers on a four-compartment region.

biology.observable: Change in regional ion amount and net ion transfer across its boundary over the same interval.
biology.finding: Perfused rat hearts lost 139 ± 12 μmol of K⁺ per g dry weight in effluent over 40 min. Tissue depletion was measured in separate hearts, leaving the within-heart balance open. [Kuki et al., Figs. 3–4](https://doi.org/10.1161/01.RES.67.2.401)

claims.title: Balanced reactions preserve a weighted inventory
claims.statement: If each reaction balances an integer-weighted inventory, the combined update preserves that inventory for any signed real reaction extents.
assumptions: The species and reaction sets at the site are finite. Each species change equals its signed stoichiometric coefficients times the extents, summed over reactions.

numerical.result: The enzyme example compared four stored species changes with the declared coefficients and two nonzero extents across one CPU half-step.

biology.observable: Amount of a specified conserved chemical group across all its species at a closed site.
biology.finding: The measured G6P + F6P pool fell 0.613357 mM (7.31%) in the first of five time courses. The raw acquisition lists 0.950 mL and different timing from the workbook. Volumes, shared calibration and unobserved pools limit the amount balance. [Eicher et al., Fig. 5](https://www.mdpi.com/2218-1989/2/4/818) · [Publisher’s workbook](https://mdpi-res.com/metabolites/metabolites-02-00818/article_deploy/metabolites-02-00818-s001.zip)
biology.unit: fmol for the target inventory, mM for the measured soluble pool

claims.title: Passive equilibrium constants multiply to one around a closed reaction cycle
claims.statement: When signed reaction extents return every species to its starting amount, their standard free-energy changes sum to zero. For signed integer traversals the product of the equilibrium constants raised to those powers is one (Wegscheider’s condition). An independent energy offset on one reaction leaves a residual equal to the offset times that reaction’s signed extent.
assumptions: At one site each passive route uses the products-minus-reactants column of a finite integer stoichiometric matrix. Each species has one dimensionless standard potential μ°/(RT). All routes use the same temperature and standard concentration. The cycle balances every species, including any explicitly represented ligand.

For positive activities, the equilibrium constant is the product-to-reactant activity quotient at zero affinity, exp(−ΔG°/RT). The Cells rate uses the reciprocal as its reverse multiplier. A negative traversal uses the reciprocal equilibrium constant. The cycle has no external work or chemostat exchange.
The proof uses exact arithmetic and holds for any values of the shared potentials. Determining their accuracy requires independent equilibrium measurements.

numerical.result: A compiled comparison would need the equilibrium quotients for all routes in one closed passive loop and a roundoff allowance for their product.

biology.observable: Independently determined equilibrium activity quotients for all reactions in one cycle at matched temperature, pH, free Mg and ionic strength.

evidence.locator: pp. 405–406, calorimetric equilibrium and thermodynamic cycle.
evidence.context: A measured glutaminase equilibrium and literature glutamine-synthetase equilibria were combined at 37 °C.
evidence.uncertainty: The quoted uncertainty belongs to the derived reaction under its stated Mg convention.
evidence.assessment: For the specific MgATP to MgADP and hydrogen phosphate reaction the inferred standard energy was −7.0 ± 0.17 kcal/mol. The synthetase leg came from other investigators.

evidence.locator: Combined acetate kinase and phosphate acetyltransferase equilibrium, pp. 6966–6972.
evidence.context: At pH 7.0, 38 °C and ionic strength 0.25 M the authors combined their equilibrium measurement with a prior acetyl-CoA hydrolysis energy.
evidence.uncertainty: Free Mg and transformed nucleotide species materially change the reported standard energy.
evidence.assessment: ATP hydrolysis at 1 mM free Mg gave −31.80 kJ/mol. The ATP–citrate lyase equilibrium was derived using the ATP result.

pairs.assumption: Independent equilibrium constants for all legs of one matched ATP reaction cycle give a product of one.
pairs.independence: Different laboratories supplied the primary measurements. Both reconstructions use literature legs, and the Mg species, ionic strength and temperature differ.
pairs.comparison: Both routes infer a favourable ATP hydrolysis energy. Benzinger combined its glutaminase data with earlier synthetase measurements. Guynn combined a coupled equilibrium with an earlier acetyl-CoA value and used the resulting ATP value to derive the citrate-lyase equilibrium.

replay.assessment: A quantitative Wegscheider residual requires independent constants for every edge at common activities and uncertainties. The exact identity in Cells remains proved.

claims.title: Binding and catalysis conserve enzyme and substrate
claims.statement: In E + S ⇌ C and C → E + P, total enzyme is E + C and total substrate is S + C + P. Omitting the returned E loses one enzyme unit per catalytic event while preserving substrate.
assumptions: Each complex carries one enzyme unit and one substrate unit. Each product retains one substrate unit. The site has no external supply or removal.

numerical.result: Lean checked both fixture columns and both weight rows. The largest absolute inventory residual in the CPU half-step was about 1.12 × 10⁻²⁰ fmol, below the 6.94 × 10⁻¹⁸ fmol tolerance. The engine refused the missing-enzyme reaction.

biology.observable: Free enzyme, substrate, bound complex and product amounts in a specified closed enzyme preparation.
biology.finding: NMR resolved ligand states bound to triosephosphate isomerase. Testing both balances requires simultaneous amounts of free enzyme, substrate, bound complex and product during turnover. [Rozovsky and McDermott, Figs. 3–5](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1794347/)

claims.title: Finite binding forms have normalized Boltzmann weights
claims.statement: At fixed free ligand activities, the fraction in each form equals its effective Boltzmann weight divided by the finite partition sum. Isomers with the same ligand counts can be combined into one registered form by summing their weights. This preserves their aggregate occupancy at every such set of activities.
assumptions: A binder has finitely many present forms and a positive total. Equilibrium is conditional on finite positive free ligand activities and a fixed positive inverse temperature. The tissue solver supplies those activities when only totals are given.

Counts relative to the base form may be signed. All standard potentials use the same temperature and standard concentration. The engine uses ideal concentration activities x/c₀. A concentration-dependent activity coefficient would require its own model.
Microscopic states within a registered form have the same ligand counts. Each state is counted once, and the group’s standard potential is −log Σ exp(−μᵢ°/RT) in units of RT.

numerical.result: On both NumPy and JIT-compiled JAX CPU, 536 form fractions across 80 S1–S7 states agreed with an 80-digit standard-potential partition to within 7.78 × 10⁻¹⁶ in absolute fraction. All 52 padded entries were zero. The six-form H/Mg tissue read stayed within the registered tolerance. The isomer control distinguished 1/2, 2/3 and 4/5 occupied.

biology.observable: ATP fraction carrying Mg at measured free Mg, pH, temperature and solution composition. The individual H/Mg microscopic forms would require additional resolved measurements.
biology.finding: At pH 7.2 and 37 °C, transferring an independently measured apparent affinity between two preparations underpredicted Mg-bound ATP by about 0.17. Their solution compositions and measurement methods differ.

evidence.locator: Rightmost marker in Figure 1, about 230 µM free Mg and a bound/unbound ATP ratio of 8.7. Dividing the ratio by one plus the ratio gives the observed fraction.
evidence.context: Three mM ATP in MOPS/KCl at pH 7.2, 37 °C and ionic strength 0.15 M. Matched aliquots supplied the fluorescent free-Mg and phosphorus NMR measurements. The two-form prediction uses Zhang et al.’s macroelectrode Kd at the same pH and temperature in a muscle-like solution of ionic strength 0.156 M. [Zhang et al. (1997)](https://doi.org/10.1006/abio.1997.2238)
fit: Zhang et al. apparent Kd at pH 7.2, 87.4 µM
evaluation: Ward et al. Figure 1 rightmost aggregate Mg-bound fraction
excluded: Ward et al. same-figure fitted Kd, 27.7 µM
Zhang et al. pH 6.7 and 7.7 Kd values
evidence.uncertainty: Zhang et al. report SD 4.9 µM over four measurements. Graph-reading precision is about ±5 µM in free Mg and ±0.1 in bound/unbound ratio. Ward et al. give no sampling uncertainty for this individual marker.
evidence.assessment: A single transferred apparent Kd misses the aggregate fraction in this preparation. Quantitative validation of individual H/Mg occupancies requires matched solution conditions and form-resolved evidence.

evidence.citation: Zhang et al. (1997), normal muscle-like solution at pH 7.2
evidence.locator: Primary report, pH 7.2 in the normal muscle-like background. Numerical series in the linked manifest.
evidence.context: Mg-sensitive macroelectrode with EDTA calibration, 37 °C and ionic strength 0.156 M.
fit: Apparent Mg–ATP affinity used for the Ward prediction
evidence.uncertainty: SD 4.9 µM across four measurements.
evidence.assessment: The apparent dissociation constant was 87.4 µM. This supplied the external affinity used to predict Ward’s aggregate Mg-bound ATP fraction.

pairs.assumption: A single apparent Mg–ATP dissociation constant transfers between these near-matched pH and temperature conditions.
pairs.independence: Zhang’s group measured free Mg using a macroelectrode. Ward’s group used matched fluorescence and phosphorus-NMR aliquots. Its regression and plotted point use the same experiment.
pairs.comparison: At pH 7.2 and 37 °C, apparent Kd was 87.4 ± 4.9 µM (SD, n = 4) in the muscle-like medium and 27.7 ± 0.4 µM (reported fit error) in MOPS/KCl. This 3.16-fold difference matters for occupancy. Ionic composition and assay differ, so the cause remains unresolved.

replay.assessment: Each preparation’s fitted affinity changes the predicted occupancy. The different ionic media give different apparent Kd, with no common independently specified binding parameters for a transfer test.

claims.title: Total ligand increases with its own free concentration
claims.statement: At fixed binder totals and other free ligand concentrations, increasing one free ligand strictly increases its total. The matrix of derivatives of totals with respect to free log concentrations is symmetric positive definite. Filling unheld coordinates with the engine’s identity block preserves this property. With the same binder totals and other free ligands fixed, the increase in total ligand is at least the increase between any two positive free concentrations.
assumptions: Each binder has finitely many present equilibrium forms with normalized weights. Temperature and standard potentials are fixed. Ligand counts relative to the base form may be signed.

Free concentrations are positive and binder totals are nonnegative. The derivative varies one free log concentration while holding the other free concentrations fixed. The formula uses exact real arithmetic.

numerical.result: NumPy, compiled JAX CPU and the differentiated conservation residual each matched all 303 entries of an 80-digit centered covariance across 80 S1–S7 states. The largest absolute error was 2.45 × 10⁻¹⁴ mM. All nine proton-release states had a negative H–Mg entry and a positive Mg diagonal. Checks included empty binders, unheld coordinates and a missing-covariance control. For free ligand of 0.25–4 mM and a single site with Kd = 1 mM, four finite total/free increment ratios matched the analytical values on compiled CPU. The empty buffer gave equality at each step. With 2 mM binder the ratios ranged from 2.067 to 1.133.

biology.observable: ATP Mg occupancy and proton release during Mg titration, and the paired change in measured total and ionized calcium at fixed bovine albumin concentration.
biology.unit: change in fraction of ATP carrying Mg
biology.finding: Independent albumin experiments show total calcium rising by at least the free-calcium increment. The total-Mg slope and fixed-pH proton response in the separate ATP system remain open.

evidence.locator: Distinct squares at approximately 130 and 230 µM free Mg have bound/unbound ATP ratios of 4.2 and 8.7. These give Mg occupancies of 0.808 and 0.897.
evidence.context: Fixed 3 mM ATP at pH 7.2, 37 °C and ionic strength 0.15 M. Matched aliquots at each level supplied free Mg by fluorescence and aggregate occupancy by phosphorus NMR. The engine’s two-form comparison uses an independent apparent affinity from a muscle-like solution. [Zhang et al.](https://doi.org/10.1006/abio.1997.2238)
fit: Zhang et al. apparent Mg–ATP Kd of 87.4 µM at 37 °C and pH 7.2
evaluation: Change in ATP Mg occupancy between the two Figure 1 samples
excluded: Ward’s fitted line and all other markers
evidence.uncertainty: Reading precision is about ±5 µM and ±0.1 in bound/unbound ratio. The figure pools seven runs and gives no pointwise sampling errors, run identities or measured total Mg.
evidence.assessment: The model gives the observed direction and overpredicts the increase by 3.7 percentage points. Solution compositions differ. The H–Mg cross-response remains open.

evidence.locator: The ATP curve and accompanying text record a pH decrease as magnesium salt was added to a 2.5 mM ATP solution.
evidence.context: The controlled variable was added magnesium salt. Bulk pH could change during the titration.
evidence.uncertainty: Figure 2 gives no free-Mg measurement or proton-equivalent count. A temperature specific to the titration could not be verified.
evidence.assessment: The acidification supports the direction of proton release in this ATP preparation. A fixed-pH measurement is still needed to quantify the cross-response.

evidence.locator: Table 1, retentate after filtration, ionized and total calcium columns
evidence.context: Bovine albumin 4.97 g/dL in retentate at 37 °C. Paired ion-selective electrode and atomic-absorption determinations.
evidence.uncertainty: Duplicate ionized readings, other entries based on at least four measurements. Reported assay CVs 2.6% for ionized and 2.1% for total calcium. Pointwise errors and free Mg are unavailable.
evidence.assessment: At five dose levels total Ca increased from 1.03 to 3.23 mM and ionized Ca from 0.45 to 1.56 mM. Each of the four successive increases in total exceeded the corresponding free increment.

evidence.citation: Günther and Ising (1998), Table 1, rows C and D
evidence.locator: Table 1, rows C and D, second page of the paper, Magnesium-Bulletin 20 (1998)
evidence.context: 40 g/L bovine albumin with 2.7 mM palmitate at 37 °C. Ion-selective electrode and atomic absorption.
evidence.uncertainty: Nine measurements per condition pooled across a magnesium-addition series (0.2–4.15 mM). Values for free calcium are means ± SEM. No sampling error for total calcium is given.
evidence.assessment: At pH 7.324 and 7.323, free Ca rose from 0.416 ± 0.008 to 1.934 ± 0.023 mM and total Ca from 0.523 to 2.605 mM. The endpoint ratio was 1.37. Pooling across Mg additions limits a fixed-free-Mg interpretation.

pairs.assumption: At fixed albumin concentration near neutral pH, increasing measured free calcium by a finite amount requires at least as large an increase in total calcium.
pairs.independence: Besarab’s and Günther’s groups independently measured free Ca with an ion-selective electrode and total Ca by atomic absorption. Each comparison stays within one albumin preparation.
pairs.comparison: All four adjacent steps in the 4.97 g/dL series satisfy Δtotal ≥ Δfree > 0 (endpoint ratio 1.98). The pH-matched 4.0 g/dL pair with palmitate gives 1.37. Both support finite buffering in those solutions. Neither provides a slope at measured, fixed free Mg or an ATP proton–Mg cross-response.

replay.assessment: The general native buffering response has Δtotal/Δfree ≥ 1 at fixed other free ligands. Both experimental calcium increments satisfy it. Albumin site parameters and free Mg at both endpoints were not measured for a preparation-matched magnitude.

claims.title: Prescribed totals admit at most one binding equilibrium
claims.statement: With fixed binder inventories, ligand totals determine at most one positive free concentration vector. Along any nonconstant joint change of free log concentrations, the projected change in totals is strictly positive. Fixing the unheld free concentrations gives the same uniqueness result for the held ligand equations and for any measured group of binder forms.
assumptions: Each binder has a finite nonempty set of equilibrium forms with fixed standard potentials at one temperature. Integer ligand counts relative to the base may be signed. Zero binder totals are allowed.
The free concentrations are positive. The equations use ideal concentration activities in a common mM frame. The candidate states have identical binder totals and fixed unheld free concentrations.
Uniqueness is conditional on existence in exact arithmetic. Admissibility of arbitrary totals, rates of approach to equilibrium and the finite Newton iteration budget require separate checks.

numerical.result: All 423 full pairs had positive projected changes on NumPy and compiled JAX CPU. With selected coordinates fixed, 283 of 284 distinct pairs were distinguishable. One pair near 0.5 mM free Mg gave equal float64 totals on both paths and a positive 80-digit projection. Both backends recovered all 423 independently manufactured target states within 2.99 × 10⁻¹³ in log concentration.

biology.observable: The concentration of a bound form after two preparations with identical totals approach equilibrium from opposite starting states. Fe–Tar absorbance supplies one such observable.
biology.unit: µM difference in Fe–Tar complex between preparation histories
biology.finding: Opposite iron-loading histories converged to the same Fe–Tar signal within the graph’s resolution. Free metal and the individual protonation states remain unmeasured.

evidence.citation: Cortes et al. (2017), supporting Fig. S4a, p. S-15
evidence.locator: The Fe–Tar concentration read from the two late traces is about 22.5 µM in both cases. They approach a common plateau by approximately 15–20 min and stay close through 90 min.
evidence.context: The final solutions had 30.8 µM Fe(II), 72 µM Tar and 220 µM EGTA at pH 7.2. Fe started bound to Tar or to EGTA, giving initial Fe–Tar signals near 31 or 0 µM. Absorbance at 720 nm measured the Fe–Tar complex across its protonation states.
evaluation: Difference between late Fe–Tar plateau readings in the two mixing directions
excluded: Absolute binding affinities and the rate of approach to the plateau
evidence.uncertainty: Each trace is readable to about ±0.5 µM, giving about ±1 µM for their difference. The figure supplies no endpoint sampling uncertainty, replicate count or figure-specific temperature.
evidence.assessment: The observed difference was indistinguishable from zero at plot resolution. One resolved complex supports the history-independent prediction in this preparation. The complete free ligand vector and Mg–ATP remain open.

claims.title: Which ligand totals admit a positive binding equilibrium?
claims.statement: A finite binding ensemble has exactly one positive equilibrium if and only if every normalized nonnegative weighting of the held ligands leaves strictly positive room above the lowest projected binder inventories. Fixing the unheld activities gives the same criterion on the held rows. Positive held totals guarantee feasibility whenever each binder has a zero-count base form.
assumptions: The model uses ideal activities, finite standard log weights, nonnegative binder totals and a finite nonempty set of chemically present forms per binder. Relative ligand counts are signed integers.
Free concentrations are exponentials of finite real log concentrations in a common mM frame. Each unheld free concentration is fixed and positive.

The existence proof uses every nonnegative direction in the unit simplex. The finite vertex claim proves the reduction for one and two ligands and for common lowest forms in any dimension. Engine enumeration and the finite Newton budget receive separate implementation checks.

numerical.result: Across the 80 registered states, both CPU backends agreed with independent binder allocations on all 236 nonempty held-coordinate projections and all four C4 challenge cases. At float64 resolution both kernels admitted an exact zero margin and refused a positive margin of 2⁻⁵⁴ mM. NumPy also admitted a negative margin of −2⁻⁵³ mM which compiled JAX CPU refused. The current tissue parser rejects nonpositive H inventories.

biology.observable: Saturation of a measured bound-complex signal as metal is added to a known ligand inventory. Testing the strict equilibrium margin would require independent free ligand measurements.
biology.finding: An Fe–Par titration shows optical saturation. The same breakpoint was used to calibrate the ligand stock, and free iron was unmeasured.

evidence.citation: Cortes et al. (2017), supporting Fig. S3b and p. S-4
evidence.locator: At pH 7.1 the trace reads about 0.39 at Fe:Par ratios of approximately 0.5 and 0.8.
evidence.context: The authors added Fe(II) to 40 µM Par in 50 mM Na–MOPS and 100 mM NaCl. The two ratios correspond to about 20 and 32 µM added Fe(II).
evaluation: Shape of the bound-complex signal during titration
excluded: An independently measured binding stoichiometry, free iron concentration, or threshold for strictly positive free ligand
evidence.uncertainty: Approximate graph readings. The panel reports no endpoint uncertainty, replicate count or measurement temperature.
evidence.assessment: The optical plateau is consistent with finite ligand capacity. Assigning one Fe per two ligands also set the working ligand concentration, so the endpoint cannot independently establish the stoichiometric boundary.

claims.title: Finite vertex tests for binding equilibria
claims.statement: For one held ligand the feasibility margin has one direction. For two, its minimum over all real normalized weights occurs at a simplex endpoint or a rational crossing of two forms of the same binder. In any number of dimensions, if each binder has a form attaining its lowest count in every held row simultaneously, the smallest coordinate remainder gives the exact minimum.
assumptions: Each binder has finitely many chemically present forms with signed integer counts relative to its base. Weights are nonnegative and sum to one on the held ligands.

The equilibrium equivalences use nonnegative binder totals, strictly positive free concentrations and finite fixed standard log weights. In the two-ligand proof duplicate or parallel profiles and coincident crossings are allowed.

The arbitrary-dimensional corner criterion requires a simultaneous componentwise minimum for each binder. The registered three-ligand S6 counts satisfy this hypothesis. The host caps on enumeration and the precision of the float64 margin are implementation properties.

numerical.result: The exact minima matched the frozen references on all 80 registered states. NumPy and compiled JAX CPU agreed with the rounded exact margins on all 236 nonempty held projections. Lean checked 31 fixture statements from the engine lists and form counts. Both backends found the negative −1/24 mM minimum in two controls where omitting one vertex would give a positive result. The earlier signed-total rounding failures remain recorded under equilibrium feasibility.

biology.observable: The finite directions follow from the model’s form counts. Experiments measure free and bound ligand at fixed inventories, as described under the linked equilibrium claim.
biology.unit: mM for the associated concentration measurements

claims.title: One-site binding follows the free ligand concentration
claims.statement: At equilibrium the occupied fraction of sites is c / (Kd + c), where c is free ligand concentration and Kd is the dissociation constant. The normalized weights of the two binder forms give the same fraction.
assumptions: One ligand binds one site. Each binder has a free and a singly occupied form, with positive total sites and positive association and dissociation rates. Kd is their off-rate divided by their on-rate.
Both concentrations are expressed in mM. The rate-balance theorem allows zero free ligand. The log-weight theorem uses positive free ligand and a positive Kd.

numerical.result: Across thirteen manufactured S1 states, the largest absolute occupancy difference from the independent reference was 3.33 × 10⁻¹⁶. Using total ligand in the same formula failed all thirteen. The first state also passed through the tissue’s stage read.

biology.observable: Equilibrium bound fraction across a free ligand titration at specified temperature and solution conditions.
biology.finding: For oxygen binding to human myoglobin at 10 °C, two digitized points set the affinity. The other three gave a root-mean-square error of 0.0422 in fractional occupancy. All five come from one figure with unknown pointwise uncertainty. [Rossi-Fanelli and Antonini, Fig. 2](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/13584010/) · [Digitized points](https://bi1.caltech.edu/2017/code/t05_nonlinear_regression.html)

evidence.locator: Fig. 2, Table I and the 10 °C figure digitization.
evidence.context: Purified human myoglobin at pH 7.45 in Tris. Equilibrium oxygen pressure sets free oxygen within this medium.
evidence.uncertainty: The five readings come from one figure with no pointwise uncertainty. Two were chosen for a retrospective fit.
evidence.assessment: The original table gives P50 about 0.324 Torr. The two-point fit gives 0.3311 Torr and native binding gives RMSE 0.0422 for the other three points.
evaluation: Digitized points 2, 3 and 5 from the same figure

evidence.locator: Table 1 and the multiwavelength oxygen-equilibrium series.
evidence.context: Equine myoglobin equilibrated against 16 known gas mixtures. The fit corrected for metmyoglobin.
evidence.uncertainty: The 37 °C affinity is a fitted parameter. Independently scored equine point uncertainties are unavailable in this comparison.

pairs.assumption: Purified mammalian myoglobin has an approximately single-site oxygen equilibrium curve when each preparation supplies its own affinity.
pairs.independence: Distinct human and equine preparations, spectroscopic methods and laboratories. The published digitization of the human figure is a reading of that one experiment.
pairs.comparison: Human myoglobin at 10 °C gave an apparent P50 near 0.32 Torr. The equine study fitted a single-site curve at pH 7.0, with P50 2.39 Torr at 37 °C.

claims.title: Uncharged membrane insertion dissipates nonnegative capacitor heat
claims.statement: The exact network heat in pJ is (10¹²/2) times the sum of C(ΔV)² + ΔC(V + ΔV)² over patches and every allocated patch share is nonnegative. For a single patch against a held bath, the heat is (10¹²/2) C V² ΔC/(C + ΔC) and the bath supplies zero image charge during insertion.
assumptions: Inserted membrane arrives uncharged. Each free node keeps its charge and each held node keeps its potential. The network is finite and the voltage changes obey its capacitor equations.
C and ΔC are nonnegative, expressed in F, with positive starting C in the one-patch formula. V and ΔV are in volts. The proof uses real arithmetic.

numerical.result: Both versions passed all seven half-step cases and completed the original extreme one-patch rollout. At ΔC/C = 1.7 × 10¹⁶ both booked +0.051603097344170144 pJ, against +0.05160309734417014 pJ from the 80-digit calculation. The earlier refusal and diagnostic substitutions are retained below.

biology.observable: Membrane capacitance, patch voltage and clamp charge during a characterized insertion event, with the incoming membrane’s initial charge accounted for.
biology.finding: Capacitance steps were measured during secretion in chromaffin cells. Testing insertion heat also needs the initial charge of the added membrane and independent electrical work and energy measurements. [Neher and Marty](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.79.21.6712)
biology.unit: pJ for heat, C for image charge

claims.title: Molecule entry scales with reservoir activity and assembly size, and exit with species count
claims.statement: For species i, each molecule in an assembly adds kᵢ to its exit rate. Entry occurs at kᵢθᵢN, where θᵢ = Kᵢρᵢ and N is total size. Balancing every species’ entry and exit at a nonempty state requires Σθᵢ = 1. With a common positive leave constant, the mean-field fractions are stationary at xᵢ = θᵢ/Σθⱼ during growth. Unequal leave constants can move the fractions away from those proportions.
assumptions: The well-mixed assembly has finitely many species with integer counts. The transfer constants Kᵢ, held activities ρᵢ and leave constants kᵢ are positive. Exchange has no catalytic multiplier and time is nominal.
A species’ instantaneous net rate is its entry rate minus its exit rate at the same state. The mean-field fraction derivative uses these rates for the count derivatives and requires N > 0.

numerical.result: Compiled rates agreed with rational reference values across all 165 three-species compositions through size eight. Doubling one species’ held activity doubled its entry and preserved the other rates. At equal counts (1, 1) and θ = (1, 1), the first fraction’s mean-field derivative was zero with leave constants (1, 1) and −¼ per nominal time unit with (1, 2).

biology.observable: Loss of accessible lipid during washout and uptake of a specified lipid as free monomer activity and individual vesicle size vary.
biology.unit: s⁻¹ for washout, M⁻¹ s⁻¹ per molar vesicles for the insertion constant
biology.finding: Accessible fluorescent lipid washed out of 310 protein-free vesicles at 0.0108 ± 0.0045 s⁻¹ (24 °C, mean ± SD). The retained fraction was 49.5 ± 8.5%. In a separate sterol assay, adding more equal-sized vesicles increased transfer at 25 °C. The insertion constant fitted at 35 °C was (6.4 ± 0.6) × 10⁷ M⁻¹ s⁻¹ per molar vesicles. Individual vesicle size, free monomer activity and the Cells time scale remain open. [Veit et al., Fig. 2 and Extended Data Fig. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41594-026-01821-8) · [Estronca et al., Fig. 2 and Table 1](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2098731/)

claims.title: Single-molecule exchange heat equals the change in assembly log weight
claims.statement: For entry between two nonempty compositions, the logarithm of the entry rate divided by the reverse exit rate at arrival equals the change in the assembly’s log weight. Reversing the event reverses the heat. At extinction the engine assigns the empty state log weight zero, so the last molecule of type i books −ln θᵢ.
assumptions: The uncatalyzed assembly exchanges one molecule at a time with positive activities and rate constants. For N > 0 the composition weight is (N−1)! times the product of θᵢ^(nᵢ)/nᵢ! over all species, where θᵢ = Kᵢρᵢ.
The empty state has zero entry propensity. Its terminal booking uses the change in log weight. The theorem concerns individual transfers in exact arithmetic.

numerical.result: Across 357 reversible pairs the largest difference from the independent log-weight change was 4.53 × 10⁻¹⁶ kBT. Two seeded lineages exercised three divisions and a terminal exit. Their saved log weight, heat, fission work and discarded free energy agreed with the independent calculation within 1.78 × 10⁻¹⁵ kBT.

biology.observable: Single-molecule entry and reverse exit rates at known neighboring compositions, with an independent transfer free-energy difference under the same conditions.

claims.title: Pair-consistent catalysis preserves the heat of a reversible transfer
claims.statement: A molecule entering an assembly sees the same catalytic multiplier as its reverse exit when the moving molecule is excluded from both catalyst counts. The log ratio of the two rates then equals the base exchange log-weight change. A singleton’s exit has multiplier one.
assumptions: The species set is finite. The counts are nonnegative integers and the catalytic matrix β has nonnegative entries. The assembly exchanges one molecule at a time, with positive rate and transfer constants and fixed positive reservoir activities.
The reversible transfer connects two nonempty compositions. The singleton’s exit into the empty state is a separate boundary case. Lean evaluates the sums in exact arithmetic.

numerical.result: The 210 ordinary transfer pairs agreed with the base heat within 5.00 × 10⁻¹⁶ kBT. Two admitted one-event runs with a large diagonal coefficient lost the remaining catalyst in the reverse sum. The passive ledger refused both, booking 2.33 × 10⁻¹⁰ and 0.693147 kBT where the exact heat is zero. Both one-event controls passed. The failure is recorded for version 1. An in-place change altered registered results and was reverted. The lead assigned the accurate reverse calculation to version 2. [Version decision](../../docs/DECISIONS.md#L8017) · [Branch replay](../PROGRESS.md#remaining-numerical-findings)

biology.observable: Entry, reverse exit and independent affinity for the same lipid as the surrounding membrane composition changes.
biology.unit: M⁻¹ s⁻¹ per molar vesicles for entry, s⁻¹ for exit
biology.finding: For the same lipid tracer at 308 K, changing pure POPC vesicles to 1:1 POPC/cholesterol halved the fitted entry constant. Exit estimates were 25 ± 2 and 27 ± 2 s⁻¹. Independent titrations gave association constants of 1.3 × 10⁹ and 6.1 × 10⁸ M⁻¹. A shared catalytic multiplier at fixed affinity cannot explain the change. The fit used the equilibrium measurement, and molecular neighbor counts remain unknown. [Sampaio et al., Table 1](https://doi.org/10.1529/biophysj.104.054007)

claims.title: Single-event catalysis can give different forward and reverse cycle rate products
claims.statement: The single-event rule evaluates the moving species’ multiplier at each event’s departure state. This adds the log ratio of two composition-dependent multipliers to the base heat. A rank-one β with only β_AA = 1 gives a four-transfer cycle ratio of 81/80. If adding one to every entry of β gives a positive rank-one matrix, the extra heat is a difference of state values and sums to zero around closed paths.
assumptions: The assembly exchanges with a held reservoir and each reversible edge joins nonempty states. Base propensities and multipliers are positive on the edges in the cycle.

The explicit square starts with one molecule each of A and B and follows +A, +B, −A, −B. The sufficient rank-one condition is 1 + βᵢⱼ = uᵢvⱼ. Then the correction to the base log weight is −ln(Σⱼ vⱼnⱼ / N).

numerical.result: The CPU agreed with rational forward and reverse rate products on 81 four-step cycles across three matrices. The rank-one β example gave 81/80. With a rank-one entrywise shift, all 27 cycles had ratio one in the exact reference and all 70 CPU edges matched the corrected log weight within 4.45 × 10⁻¹⁶ kBT. The lead corrected the design and assigned the matching code wording to the builder. [Design correction](https://github.com/Eidosoma/Cells/blob/0b564f2d99f70995c741456d7f55a515d049dd4d/docs/GARD_DESIGN.md#L320)

biology.observable: Forward and reverse transition rates around the same four known lipid compositions under a fixed reservoir, including the identity of the moving lipid.

claims.title: Whole-molecule counts set the ideal mixing cost of membrane entry
claims.statement: For a membrane with N molecules and a molecules of the incoming species, the activity for adding one molecule relative to its standard state is (a + 1)/(N + 1 − c). A finite source pool also contributes its count and standard concentration to the transfer energy.
assumptions: The ideal term uses log factorials of integer counts. The measure offset c is 0 or 1. For N ≥ c the activity formula applies directly. The first insertion into an empty membrane has only the entering species’ standard energy.
The equilibrium experiment measures bulk activity relative to cholesterol crystals. The ideal bulk curve is A = s x with one fitted reference-state scale s and cholesterol mole fraction x.

numerical.result: Both registered measures agreed with exact-factorial state weights on 592 compositions in the ideal-only world, within 2.14 × 10⁻¹⁴ kBT. Reference rates and independent ledger replay passed. At equal A and B counts with N = 6 the insertion activities were 4/7 and 4/6.

biology.observable: Equilibrium cholesterol activity as a function of membrane mole fraction.
biology.unit: dimensionless activity relative to crystalline cholesterol

pairs.assumption: Increasing the cholesterol mole fraction of a dilute DOPC membrane raises its equilibrium cholesterol activity.
pairs.independence: Different groups equilibrated their own DOPC vesicles against cyclodextrin. They share an assay principle. Only Shaw calibrated activities against crystals.
pairs.comparison: Shaw’s crystal-referenced activity rose from 0.10 ± 0.01 at 5.4 mol% to 0.22 ± 0.02 at 11.4 mol% (68% intervals). In Lange’s 25 °C data the distribution coefficient changed little across roughly 0.6–14 mol%. Eq. 3 then gives rising cyclodextrin loading x/[(1−x)Q], a relative activity proxy at low occupancy. The pair supports the dilute trend; the high-fraction ideal law and absolute calibration remain open.

replay.assessment: The declared ideal mixing activity rises at low fraction and Shaw’s low-fraction data rise. Lange measures cyclodextrin partition. The dilute-occupancy mapping gives the same direction, without the crystal-referenced activity or bath calibration needed for a second absolute replay.

evidence.citation: Lange et al. (2013), Eq. 3 and Fig. 4A
evidence.locator: Fig. 4A, DOPC open circles, and equilibrium Eq. 3.
evidence.context: At 25 °C cholesterol was equilibrated between DOPC vesicles and methyl-β-cyclodextrin across low cholesterol mole fractions.
evidence.uncertainty: The ranges are approximate figure readings. Pointwise errors and an uncertainty on the fitted slope are unavailable. No calibration to crystalline cholesterol was reported.
evidence.assessment: The weak composition dependence of Q compared with the change in x implies increasing equilibrium bath loading in the dilute series. At low occupancy this supplies a relative activity proxy. The series ends near x = 0.14.

evidence.citation: Shaw et al. (2023), Fig. 2A and Table S1
evidence.locator: Table S1, printed page 13, gives the 25 DOPC readings and both 68% confidence half-widths.
evidence.context: Protein-free DOPC/cholesterol large unilamellar vesicles equilibrated with methyl-beta-cyclodextrin at room temperature. Activity 1 refers to crystalline cholesterol.

claims.title: Pair interactions change the energy of membrane entry with composition
claims.statement: Updating the symmetric pair energy equals recomputing it from all membrane counts. For A entering a binary membrane with b molecules of B and total N, the excess insertion energy is χb²/[N(N + 1)] and the bulk excess chemical potential is χ(b/N)².
assumptions: The pair matrix is symmetric and counts remain in their physical domain. For the binary result the diagonal is zero, χ is the unlike-pair energy in kBT and N is positive.

The bulk comparison treats the cholesterol/DOPC membrane as a homogeneous binary mixture at fixed temperature. It uses one composition-independent χ and a fitted scale for the cholesterol crystal reference.

numerical.result: Under both measures, the signed pair matrix matched the reference energy within 2.14 × 10⁻¹⁴ kBT. The reversible edge identities passed. With equal counts and χ = 1, adding A cost an extra 0.214286 kBT at N = 6 and 0.245902 at N = 60.

biology.observable: Equilibrium cholesterol activity as a function of membrane mole fraction under a binary interaction model.
biology.unit: dimensionless activity relative to crystalline cholesterol

pairs.assumption: At 37 °C, cholesterol partition favors SOPC over DOPC, so the host phospholipid affects its transfer free energy.
pairs.independence: Niu and Litman and Lange’s group collected separate equilibrium cyclodextrin–vesicle partition datasets. Both used a similar partition method. Only ratios within the same experiment and temperature are compared.

Both support the direction and approximate magnitude of this host effect. The ratios alone cannot identify the Cells pair coefficient χ or its dependence on cholesterol fraction.

replay.assessment: The native pair energy can distinguish host compositions. The observed SOPC/DOPC affinity ratios are 1.40 and 1.37. Neither measurement independently specifies the two membrane interaction energies or the bath reference for a forward prediction.

Tenchov detected a 3.40 nm diffraction line in some nominal 0.50 mixtures at 20 °C and none in other 0.50 mixtures. The observed appearances differ. Neither pair of feed fractions establishes two different equilibrium bilayer saturation fractions.
